faqs.q: Is there a minimum number of users?
faqs.a: Yes — Starter and Professional have a 3-user minimum, Enterprise a 5-user minimum. We kept it deliberately simple: no bundled 'platform packs', no forced 10-seat floor.

faqs.q: Do you cap quote revision history?
faqs.a: No. Revision history is unlimited on every tier, including Starter. A quote's Rev 0 through Rev 7 history is the record of what you agreed to — charging for it would be the wrong kind of gate.

faqs.q: Do you cap RFQ line items?
faqs.a: No. A 400-line RFQ costs the same as a 4-line one on every tier.

faqs.q: Are the India compliance features an add-on?

faqs.q: What happens when I hit a tier ceiling?

faqs.q: How does the annual discount work?
faqs.a: Annual billing is 17% below the monthly rate — $32, $41 and $82 per user per month respectively, billed yearly.

faqs.q: What is the $2,000/month Enterprise platform fee for?
faqs.a: Multi-entity infrastructure, custom data residency, the compliance dashboard, SSO, and a dedicated customer success manager with a 2-hour response SLA. Enterprise is capability-led, not a seat-count trap.

items.name: Quote editor
items.h1: Quote editor with attachments, share links, FX and revisions
items.metaTitle: Quote editor with share links and revisions
items.metaDescription: Build line-item manufacturing quotes with drawing attachments, a customer share link, locked FX rates and unlimited revision history. Live on every tier.
items.lead: The screen your estimator lives in. Line items, drawings, terms, a share link the buyer opens without a login, and a revision trail that never gets trimmed.
items.answer: The KanchanFlow quote editor is the quoting surface of our RFQ-to-Order CRM. It builds a line-item quote from an RFQ, attaches drawings and certificates, converts currency at a rate you lock onto the quote, and keeps every revision — Rev 0 through Rev 12 — permanently, on every tier including Starter.
summary: Most shops quote out of a spreadsheet that gets copied, renamed and emailed until nobody knows which file the customer actually holds. The quote editor replaces that with one record per quote and one revision chain underneath it. Each line carries a part number, description, quantity, unit price, lead time and the drawing it was priced from.

When you send it, the buyer gets a share link rather than a 6 MB attachment that bounces off their mail server. The link renders the quote in a browser, shows the attachments, records when it was opened, and stays valid until the quote expires. Nothing about that flow is gated: Starter shops get the same editor as Enterprise.

capabilities.title: Line items priced against the drawing they came from
capabilities.body: Every line can be tied to a specific drawing file and revision letter. When the customer sends Rev C of a print, the line shows which revision it was priced against, so a re-quote is a five-minute check rather than an argument.

capabilities.title: Attachments that travel with the quote
capabilities.body: Drawings, material certs, prior inspection reports and your standard terms attach to the quote itself. They appear in the share link and in the PDF, and they stay attached to every later revision unless you remove them.

capabilities.title: Share links instead of email attachments
capabilities.body: A quote sends as a browser link. The buyer opens it without an account, forwards it internally, and you see the open timestamp. No file-size bounce, no 'can you resend it, our filter ate it'.

capabilities.title: Locked FX on multi-currency quotes
capabilities.body: Quote a Canadian or Mexican customer in their currency and the rate is captured on the quote at the moment you price it. The rate does not silently drift between quote and order — you decide when to re-rate.

capabilities.title: Unlimited revision history
capabilities.body: Rev 0 through however far the job runs. We never trim revision history on any tier. The record of what you agreed to is the record — charging for it, or expiring it after ninety days, would be the wrong kind of gate.

capabilities.title: Quote expiry and validity terms
capabilities.body: Set validity in days on the quote. Expired quotes stop accepting acceptance through the share link and show as expired in the pipeline, so nobody books an order against material pricing from March.

howItWorks.name: Start from an RFQ or from scratch
howItWorks.text: Open an RFQ and press quote, or start blank for a phone enquiry. Customer, contact, delivery address and any drawings already on the RFQ carry across without retyping.

howItWorks.name: Build the lines
howItWorks.text: Add a line per part. Enter quantity, unit price, lead time and any process notes. Duplicate a line to price an alternate quantity break, or pull a line from a previous quote to the same customer.

howItWorks.name: Attach the evidence
howItWorks.text: Drop in the drawing PDF or STEP file, the material cert you will supply, and your standard terms. These become part of the quote record and appear in the buyer's share link.

howItWorks.name: Set currency, validity and terms
howItWorks.text: Choose the quote currency and lock the FX rate. Set validity in days, payment terms and any freight assumption. Everything you assumed is written on the quote, not in your head.

howItWorks.name: Send the share link
howItWorks.text: Send by email from inside the record or paste the link into WhatsApp. The buyer opens it in a browser. You get an open timestamp and can see how many times it was viewed.

howItWorks.name: Revise without losing the trail
howItWorks.text: Press revise. Rev 1 opens as a copy, you change what changed, and Rev 0 is preserved intact with its own share link and its own send history.

tierAvailability.starter: Included. Basic visual diff between revisions, unlimited revisions, unlimited line items.
tierAvailability.professional: Included. Full diff view with change alerts on price, quantity and lead time.
tierAvailability.enterprise: Included. Full diff plus custom fields on the quote header and line.

faqs.q: Can a customer accept a quote from the share link?
faqs.a: Yes. The share link carries an accept action, and on quotes routed through Aadhaar eSign the acceptance is captured as a legally valid signature. Otherwise it records the accepting contact, timestamp and IP against the quote.

faqs.q: How many revisions can a quote have?
faqs.a: As many as the job needs. We do not cap revision count or retention on any tier, including Starter. A quote that ran to Rev 11 keeps all eleven, each with its own send history.

faqs.q: What file types can I attach?
faqs.a: PDF, DWG, DXF, STEP and IGES files, plus the usual office and image formats. Storage is 10 GB on Starter, 100 GB on Professional and 500 GB or more on Enterprise.

faqs.q: Does the FX rate update automatically after I send?
faqs.a: No, and that is deliberate. The rate is locked to the quote when you price it. If you want to re-rate, you do it explicitly on a new revision so the customer sees what changed.

faqs.q: Can I see whether the buyer opened the quote?
faqs.a: Yes. The quote record shows first-open time, most recent open and view count for the share link. It does not tell you who forwarded it internally — only that the link was opened.

items.name: Invoice editor
items.h1: Invoice editor with credit and debit notes, aging and credit management
items.metaTitle: Invoice editor with credit notes and aging
items.metaDescription: Raise invoices from accepted quotes and orders, issue credit and debit notes, and watch aging and customer credit limits. Live in KanchanFlow on every tier.
items.lead: Invoices that come from the order, not from a second system. Credit notes, debit notes, an aging bucket view and a credit limit that actually blocks the next shipment.
items.answer: KanchanFlow's invoice editor closes the RFQ-to-Order CRM loop: an accepted quote becomes an order, and an order becomes an invoice without rekeying a line. It issues credit and debit notes against the original document, tracks aging in 0-30-60-90 buckets, and enforces a per-customer credit limit before the next dispatch.
summary: Shops usually invoice in the accounting package, which means the sales team cannot see what is unpaid without asking the bookkeeper. We keep invoicing next to the order so the person chasing the customer can see the balance, the aging bucket and the credit limit on the same screen as the quote history.

Invoices carry the same line structure as the order they came from, so a partial dispatch invoices partially and the balance stays visible on the order. Credit notes and debit notes reference the original invoice number rather than floating free, which is what your accountant and any auditor will ask for first.

capabilities.title: Invoice straight from the order
capabilities.body: Lines, quantities, prices, tax treatment and delivery address all carry from the order. Invoice the whole order or only the quantity that shipped — the order keeps the balance open until it is fully invoiced.

capabilities.title: Credit and debit notes with a parent reference
capabilities.body: A credit note is raised against a specific invoice and shows on both records. Short shipment, rejected parts, a price correction after the fact — each gets a note that points at the document it corrects.

capabilities.title: Aging in real buckets
capabilities.body: Current, 1-30, 31-60, 61-90 and 90-plus, per customer and in total. The aging view is the same data the salesperson sees on the account, so nobody is chasing a customer who paid last Tuesday.

capabilities.title: Credit limits that hold
capabilities.body: Set a credit limit per customer. When outstanding plus the value of the next dispatch crosses it, the order flags before the goods leave. You can override it, but somebody has to make that choice on the record.

capabilities.title: Payment recording and part payments
capabilities.body: Record full or partial payments against an invoice with a date and reference. The balance, the aging bucket and the customer's exposure all move together.

howItWorks.name: Accept the quote and open the order
howItWorks.text: An accepted quote becomes an order with the same lines. Nothing is retyped, and the quote revision the customer accepted stays linked to the order.

howItWorks.name: Dispatch some or all of it
howItWorks.text: Record what actually shipped against each line. Partial dispatch is normal in a job shop, so the order stays open with a remaining quantity per line.

howItWorks.name: Raise the invoice
howItWorks.text: Invoice the dispatched quantity. Tax treatment follows the customer record — US tax jurisdiction rates, or GST with HSN and place of supply where the India module applies.

howItWorks.name: Correct it with a note, not an edit
howItWorks.text: If the invoice is wrong after it is issued, raise a credit or debit note referencing it. The original document is never silently rewritten.

howItWorks.name: Record payment and watch the bucket
howItWorks.text: Enter payments as they land. The aging view, the customer balance and the credit-limit check all update from the same figures.

tierAvailability.starter: Included. One accounting connector of your choice for pushing invoices out.
tierAvailability.professional: Included. All three accounting connectors — Tally, Zoho Books and QuickBooks.
tierAvailability.enterprise: Included. All three connectors plus a custom ERP connector and multi-entity roll-up.

faqs.q: Does this replace QuickBooks or Tally?
faqs.a: No. We raise the customer-facing document and track what is owed; your accounting package remains the book of record. The connector pushes invoices, credit notes and payments across so the two do not drift.

faqs.q: Can I invoice a partial dispatch?
faqs.a: Yes. Record the shipped quantity per line and invoice only that. The order stays open with the remaining quantity and can be invoiced again when the balance ships.

faqs.q: What happens when a customer goes over their credit limit?
faqs.a: The next dispatch on that account flags before it leaves. A user with the right permission can override the block, and the override is recorded against the order with a name and timestamp.

faqs.q: Can I edit an invoice after sending it?
faqs.a: You can edit an unsent draft. Once issued, corrections go through a credit or debit note that references the original. That is what keeps the trail defensible.

faqs.q: How is tax calculated?
faqs.a: From the customer record. US customers use the US tax rate and SaaS jurisdiction tables; customers under the India module get GST with GSTIN, HSN and place of supply applied automatically.

items.name: Orders
items.h1: Quote-as-Order with staged billing and partial dispatch
items.metaDescription: Turn an accepted quote into an order without rekeying, then run staged billing and partial dispatch against it. The orders module shipped 25 August 2026.
items.lead: The handoff that usually happens in email. An accepted quote becomes an order with its lines intact, and stays open until every line has shipped and been billed.
items.answer: Orders is the handoff layer of the KanchanFlow RFQ-to-Order CRM. An accepted quote becomes an order carrying its own line structure, so staged billing and partial dispatch run against the quantities the customer actually agreed to. The module shipped to production on 25 August 2026 and is included on every tier.
summary: In most shops the order does not exist as a record. There is an accepted quote, a customer PO in a mailbox, and a job traveller on the floor — and reconciling them is somebody's Friday afternoon. Orders makes the agreement itself a record: what was ordered, what has shipped, what has been billed, what is still open.

Because job shop work rarely ships in one go, the order is built around partial fulfilment from the start. Each line holds an ordered quantity, a dispatched quantity and an invoiced quantity, and those three numbers are allowed to differ. The order closes when they agree, not when someone remembers to close it.

capabilities.title: Quote-as-Order conversion
capabilities.body: The accepted quote revision becomes the order. Lines, prices, lead times, delivery address and attachments carry across, and the order keeps a permanent link back to the exact revision the customer accepted.

capabilities.title: Partial dispatch per line
capabilities.body: Ship 40 of 100 today and 60 in three weeks. Each dispatch records quantity, date and reference against the line, and the remaining quantity stays visible on the order.

capabilities.title: Staged billing
capabilities.body: Bill on advance, on dispatch, or on milestone. The order tracks invoiced value against ordered value so you can see, per line, what is still to be billed.

capabilities.title: Customer PO capture
capabilities.body: Attach the customer's purchase order to the order record and store their PO number against it, so your invoice quotes the reference their accounts payable system is looking for.

capabilities.title: Production milestone visibility
capabilities.body: Mark milestone progress manually on Starter, or take milestone updates from an ERP webhook on Professional. Enterprise rolls milestones up across plants.

capabilities.title: Open-order view for the whole team
capabilities.body: One list of every open order with dispatched, invoiced and outstanding value. It is the list you would otherwise rebuild in a spreadsheet every Monday morning.

howItWorks.name: Customer accepts a quote revision
howItWorks.text: Acceptance comes through the share link, an eSign flow, or is recorded manually when a PO lands by email. The accepted revision is stamped on the record.

howItWorks.name: Convert to an order
howItWorks.text: Press convert. The order opens with the same lines and prices. Add the customer PO number and attach their purchase order document.

howItWorks.name: Set the billing stages
howItWorks.text: Choose whether this order bills on advance, on dispatch or against milestones, and set the split. The order shows what is billable now and what is not yet.

howItWorks.name: Dispatch against lines
howItWorks.text: As parts ship, record the quantity dispatched per line with a date and a reference. The remaining quantity updates on the line and on the order header.

howItWorks.name: Invoice what shipped
howItWorks.text: Raise an invoice for the dispatched quantity. The invoiced quantity on the line moves, and the order shows the outstanding balance.

howItWorks.name: Close when the three numbers agree
howItWorks.text: When ordered, dispatched and invoiced match on every line, the order closes. Anything unmatched stays visible, which is the point.

tierAvailability.professional: Included. Milestone updates via ERP webhook, plus delivery risk alerts and freight helpers.
tierAvailability.enterprise: Included. Multi-plant milestone roll-up across entities.

faqs.q: When did the orders module ship?
faqs.a: 25 August 2026. It is listed in the changelog as a new feature release, and it is live for every tier today.

faqs.q: Can one order have several dispatches and several invoices?
faqs.a: Yes. That is the normal case. Each line tracks ordered, dispatched and invoiced quantities separately, and the order stays open until all three agree.

faqs.q: Does the order push to my ERP?
faqs.a: Professional and Enterprise can take milestone updates back from an ERP through a webhook. Pushing works order data into an ERP is a custom connector on Enterprise, not a standard feature.

faqs.q: What if the customer changes the quantity after ordering?
faqs.a: Amend the order line. The change is recorded against the order, and the linked accepted quote revision is untouched, so you can still see what was originally agreed.

faqs.q: Can I create an order without a quote?
faqs.a: Yes, for repeat or blanket business where no quote was raised. You lose the link back to an accepted revision, which the record notes.

items.name: GST invoicing
items.h1: GST invoicing with GSTIN, HSN, GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B
items.metaTitle: GST invoicing with GSTIN, HSN and GSTR returns
items.subhead: For USA manufacturers with India operations, India-based contract customers, or manufacturers exporting to India.
items.metaDescription: Raise GST-compliant invoices with GSTIN, HSN codes and place of supply, and export GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B summaries. On every tier, never an add-on.
items.lead: Correct GST treatment on the invoice at the moment you raise it — GSTIN on the header, HSN on the line, place of supply driving CGST, SGST or IGST — and returns data that reconciles.
items.answer: GST invoicing in KanchanFlow applies Indian indirect tax rules inside the RFQ-to-Order CRM: GSTIN on the party, HSN or SAC on every line, and place of supply deciding CGST and SGST or IGST. GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B summaries export from the same records. It is included on every tier and never gated.
summary: If you run a plant in Pune, buy from an Indian contract manufacturer, or ship product into India, someone in your organisation is dealing with GST. Getting it wrong is not a rounding error: a mismatched GSTIN or a wrong place of supply blocks your customer's input tax credit, and they will hold your payment until it is fixed.

We put the tax logic where the document is created rather than at month end. The party's GSTIN sets the state, the state pair sets whether the transaction is intra-state or inter-state, and the line's HSN sets the rate. By the time the invoice is issued the treatment is already decided, and the return summaries are a read of records that were correct when they were made.

capabilities.title: GSTIN on every party
capabilities.body: Customers and vendors carry a validated GSTIN with the registered legal name and state. The state code drives the place-of-supply logic on every document raised against that party.

capabilities.title: HSN and SAC at line level
capabilities.body: Each product or service line carries its own HSN or SAC code and rate. A mixed invoice with goods at one rate and machining services at another is handled on a single document.

capabilities.title: Place of supply and the CGST / SGST / IGST split
capabilities.body: Same-state supply splits into CGST and SGST; inter-state raises IGST. Export invoices are marked as such with or without payment of tax. The decision comes from the record, not from the person typing.

capabilities.title: GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B summaries
capabilities.body: Export B2B, B2C and credit or debit note data in GSTR-1 shape, and the summary figures for GSTR-3B, straight from the invoices raised in the period. Filing still happens on the GST portal or through your filing agent.

capabilities.title: Reverse charge and exempt handling
capabilities.body: Flag reverse-charge supplies and exempt or nil-rated lines so they land in the right return bucket rather than being quietly taxed at standard rate.

howItWorks.name: Set up the party
howItWorks.text: Enter the customer's GSTIN. Validation returns the registered legal name, state and status, and the record stores the state code used for place-of-supply decisions.

howItWorks.name: Code your items
howItWorks.text: Assign an HSN code to each product and an SAC to each service you invoice. The rate attaches to the code, so it applies consistently across every quote and invoice.

howItWorks.name: Raise the invoice
howItWorks.text: The invoice compares your registered state with the place of supply and applies CGST and SGST or IGST accordingly, line by line, at the rate attached to each HSN.

howItWorks.name: Issue notes against the original
howItWorks.text: Credit and debit notes reference the parent invoice and carry the same GST treatment, so they reconcile in the return rather than appearing as loose documents.

howItWorks.name: Pull the return data
howItWorks.text: At period end, export the GSTR-1 detail and the GSTR-3B summary for the invoices raised in that period, and hand it to whoever files.

faqs.q: Why does a USA-focused CRM ship GST features?
faqs.a: Because a large share of USA manufacturers have India operations, buy from India-based contract manufacturers, or export into India. Those transactions need correct GST treatment, and bolting it on at month end does not work.

faqs.q: Is GST an add-on or a higher tier?
faqs.a: Neither. GST invoicing, GSTIN validation, e-Invoice IRN and the MSMED 43B(h) tracker are included on Starter, Professional and Enterprise. We do not gate regulatory features by price.

faqs.q: Do you file the returns for me?
faqs.a: No. We produce GSTR-1 detail and GSTR-3B summary exports from your invoices. Filing happens on the GST portal or through your chartered accountant or filing agent.

faqs.q: What happens if the customer's GSTIN is wrong?
faqs.a: Validation catches it before the invoice goes out. A GSTIN that does not resolve, or resolves to a cancelled registration, is flagged on the party record.

faqs.q: Can one invoice mix goods and services?
faqs.a: Yes. HSN and SAC codes sit at line level with their own rates, so a job that bills material and machining separately produces one correct document.

items.name: e-Invoice IRN
items.subhead: For USA manufacturers with India operations, India-based contract customers, or manufacturers exporting to India.
items.metaDescription: Generate the Invoice Reference Number and signed QR code for India e-invoicing from the invoice record, with cancellation inside the statutory window.
items.lead: Push the invoice to the Invoice Registration Portal, get the IRN and signed QR back, and print both on the document — without leaving the invoice you just raised.
items.answer: e-Invoice IRN generation registers a KanchanFlow invoice with India's Invoice Registration Portal and writes the returned Invoice Reference Number, acknowledgement number and signed QR code back onto the document. It runs from inside the RFQ-to-Order CRM rather than a separate portal upload, and is included on every tier including Starter.
summary: India's e-invoicing rules mean a B2B invoice above the applicable turnover threshold is not valid until it has been registered and carries an IRN with a signed QR code. Most shops handle this by exporting a JSON file, uploading it to a portal, and pasting the result back — which is where transposition errors and missed cancellations come from.

We do the round trip from the invoice record. When you register, the payload is built from the invoice you already raised, the response is written back onto it, and the QR code prints on the PDF. If the invoice has to be cancelled, the cancellation runs within the statutory window from the same screen, and the record shows what happened and when.

capabilities.title: IRN generation from the invoice record
capabilities.body: No JSON export, no portal login, no copy-paste. The payload is assembled from the invoice, sent for registration and the response is stored against the document.

capabilities.title: Signed QR code on the printed invoice
capabilities.body: The QR returned by the portal is written onto the invoice PDF and the share link, so the document your customer receives is the registered one.

capabilities.title: Acknowledgement number and date stored
capabilities.body: The acknowledgement number and timestamp are kept on the invoice permanently. When a customer's accounts team queries a document eighteen months later, the registration evidence is on the record.

capabilities.title: Cancellation within the statutory window
capabilities.body: Cancel a registered invoice inside the allowed period with a reason code. The cancellation and its reason are stored, and the invoice is marked cancelled rather than deleted.

capabilities.title: Failure handling that does not lose the invoice
capabilities.body: If registration is rejected, the error from the portal is shown against the invoice with the field that failed. The invoice stays as a draft you can correct and resubmit.

howItWorks.name: Raise the invoice with complete GST data
howItWorks.text: Party GSTIN, HSN codes, place of supply and values must all be present. The invoice will not submit with a missing mandatory field, which is a cheaper failure than a portal rejection.

howItWorks.name: Register it
howItWorks.text: Press generate IRN. The invoice payload is built and sent to the Invoice Registration Portal through your e-invoicing provider credentials.

howItWorks.name: Receive the IRN, acknowledgement and QR
howItWorks.text: The portal returns the Invoice Reference Number, an acknowledgement number and date, and the signed QR code. All three are written onto the invoice record.

howItWorks.name: Send the registered document
howItWorks.text: The PDF and the share link now carry the IRN and QR. That is the version your customer's accounts payable team needs for their input tax credit.

howItWorks.name: Cancel if you must, inside the window
howItWorks.text: If the invoice is wrong, cancel it with a reason code inside the statutory period and raise a corrected one. After the window closes, the correction is a credit note instead.

faqs.q: Do I need my own e-invoicing credentials?
faqs.a: Yes. Registration happens against your organisation's credentials with an authorised provider such as ClearTax. We connect to that provider; we are not the registrar.

faqs.q: Is IRN generation gated to a higher tier?
faqs.a: No. It is included on Starter, Professional and Enterprise. India regulatory features are never behind a tier on this product.

faqs.q: What happens if the portal rejects the invoice?
faqs.a: The rejection reason and the failing field are shown on the invoice, which stays editable. You fix it and resubmit — the invoice number is not burned.

faqs.q: Can I cancel an IRN after the statutory window?
faqs.a: No, and nobody can. After the window, the correction route is a credit note against the registered invoice, which our invoice editor raises with the parent reference intact.

faqs.q: Does the QR code print on the customer's copy?
faqs.a: Yes, on both the PDF and the browser share link. The registered document and the document you send are the same document.

items.name: GSTIN validation
items.subhead: For USA manufacturers with India operations, India-based contract customers, or manufacturers exporting to India.
items.metaDescription: Validate a customer or vendor GSTIN against the registry before you quote, and catch cancelled or mismatched registrations early. On every tier.
items.lead: Check the registration before the invoice, not after the payment is held. Legal name, state, registration type and current status, written onto the party record.
items.answer: GSTIN validation in KanchanFlow checks an Indian tax registration against the registry and writes the registered legal name, state, registration type and current status onto the customer or vendor record. Because the state code drives place-of-supply logic across the RFQ-to-Order CRM, validating early prevents wrong tax treatment on every later document.
summary: A GSTIN is not just an identifier on the invoice header. Its state code decides whether a supply is intra-state or inter-state, which decides whether you charge CGST and SGST or IGST. Enter it wrong and every invoice to that customer is wrong in the same way, usually until their accounts team notices and stops paying.

Validation happens when the party is created and can be re-run at any time. It returns the legal name as registered, the state, the type of registration and whether it is active, cancelled or suspended. Those facts sit on the record where the quoting and invoicing logic reads them. Validating early is a two-minute step that prevents a repeating error.

capabilities.title: Registry lookup on entry
capabilities.body: Type a GSTIN on a customer or vendor and the registered legal name, trade name, state and registration date come back. A mistyped digit fails immediately rather than three invoices later.

capabilities.title: Status checks for cancelled and suspended registrations
capabilities.body: The record shows whether the registration is active, cancelled or suspended. Supplying to a cancelled registration is a problem you want to find before the goods move.

capabilities.title: Legal name match against your record
capabilities.body: If the registered legal name does not match the customer name you typed, the mismatch is flagged. That is usually a sign you have the wrong entity in a group.

capabilities.title: State code feeding place-of-supply logic
capabilities.body: The validated state code becomes the input to CGST, SGST and IGST decisions on every quote and invoice for that party, so the treatment is consistent by construction.

capabilities.title: Re-validation on demand
capabilities.body: Registrations change. Re-run validation on a party at any time, and the record keeps the date it was last checked so nobody has to guess how stale it is.

howItWorks.name: Enter the GSTIN on the party
howItWorks.text: Add the fifteen-character registration to the customer or vendor record. Format is checked locally before any lookup is attempted.

howItWorks.name: Run the lookup
howItWorks.text: The registration is checked against the registry through your connected provider, and the response is stored on the record with a timestamp.

howItWorks.name: Review the returned facts
howItWorks.text: Registered legal name, trade name, state, registration type, date of registration and current status are shown. Mismatches against your own record are highlighted.

howItWorks.name: Accept or correct
howItWorks.text: Accept the registered legal name onto the party, or correct the GSTIN if you have the wrong entity. The state code is written to the record either way.

howItWorks.name: Re-check when it matters
howItWorks.text: Before a large order, or on a periodic review of your customer base, re-run validation. The record shows the last-checked date so you know what you are trusting.

faqs.a: It runs when a GSTIN is first entered, and you can re-run it on demand. We do not silently re-validate your whole customer base in the background.

faqs.q: What if a registration is cancelled after I have quoted?
faqs.a: Re-validate the party. The status updates on the record, and you can decide whether to proceed. We flag it; the commercial decision is yours.

faqs.a: Yes. The same validation runs on vendor records, which matters for the MSMED 43B(h) tracker where supplier classification depends on the registration.

items.name: Aadhaar eSign
items.h1: Legally valid quote acceptance via Aadhaar eSign
items.subhead: For USA manufacturers with India operations, India-based contract customers, or manufacturers exporting to India.
items.metaDescription: Close a quote with a legally valid Aadhaar eSign signature instead of an email that says yes. Signature, timestamp and audit trail attach to the revision.
items.lead: Turn 'approved, go ahead' in an email thread into a signed document with an audit trail, without printing, scanning or couriering anything.
items.answer: Aadhaar eSign lets an Indian buyer sign a KanchanFlow quote from its share link and produces a legally valid electronic signature under India's IT Act. The signed document, signer identity, timestamp and audit trail attach to the exact quote revision that was accepted, inside the RFQ-to-Order CRM rather than a separate signing tool.
summary: Acceptance evidence is where quote-to-order disputes start. An email saying 'go ahead' is not a signature, a scanned and couriered PO takes a week, and a third-party signing tool leaves the signed PDF in a system your CRM cannot see. When the customer later disputes a price or a quantity, you are reconstructing the story from a mailbox.

With Aadhaar eSign, the buyer opens the quote share link, signs through the OTP flow against their Aadhaar-linked identity, and the signed document is written back onto the quote revision. What was signed, who signed it, and when, all live on the record the order is created from. There is no separate signing system to reconcile against afterwards.

capabilities.title: Sign from the quote share link
capabilities.body: No account, no app install and no separate signing portal. The buyer opens the same browser link they were already reviewing and signs from it.

capabilities.title: Signature bound to a specific revision
capabilities.body: The signature attaches to Rev 3, not to 'the quote'. If a Rev 4 is later issued, the earlier signed revision stays intact with its own signed document.

capabilities.title: Signer identity and timestamp on the record
capabilities.body: The signing party's name as returned by the eSign flow, the timestamp and the transaction reference are stored on the quote. That is the evidence you need eighteen months later.

capabilities.title: Signed PDF stored against the quote
capabilities.body: The signed document is kept with the quote and carries forward to the order created from it, so the acceptance evidence travels with the commercial record.

capabilities.title: Falls back to recorded acceptance
capabilities.body: Where eSign is not appropriate, the share link still records who accepted, when, and from where. You are never forced into a signing flow that does not fit the deal.

howItWorks.name: Send the quote as a share link
howItWorks.text: The buyer receives a browser link rather than an attachment. They can review lines, drawings and terms before anything is signed.

howItWorks.name: Buyer chooses to sign
howItWorks.text: From the share view they start the eSign flow. The document presented for signature is the exact revision they are looking at.

howItWorks.name: Identity verification and OTP
howItWorks.text: The signer authenticates through the Aadhaar eSign OTP flow with the licensed e-sign service provider. We do not see or store Aadhaar numbers.

howItWorks.name: Signed document returns
howItWorks.text: The signed PDF, signer name, timestamp and transaction reference come back and are written onto the quote revision.

howItWorks.name: Convert to an order
howItWorks.text: The quote is marked accepted and can be converted to an order. The signed document stays linked to the order for the life of the job.

faqs.a: Yes, under India's Information Technology Act, when executed through a licensed e-sign service provider. We integrate with that provider rather than acting as one ourselves.

faqs.a: No. The identity verification happens with the licensed provider. We receive and store the signed document, the signer name, the timestamp and a transaction reference.

faqs.q: What about USA customers who cannot use Aadhaar?
faqs.a: They use recorded acceptance from the share link, which captures the accepting contact, timestamp and IP against the revision. Aadhaar eSign is for the India side of your business.

faqs.q: What happens if the quote is revised after signing?
faqs.a: The signed revision is preserved with its signature. A new revision starts unsigned, which is exactly what you want — a signature should never silently carry across a price change.

faqs.q: Is this an extra charge?
faqs.a: The feature is included on every tier. Your e-sign service provider may charge per signature transaction; that contract is between you and them.

items.name: Multi-currency
items.metaDescription: Quote and invoice in your customer's currency with a rate locked to the document, and roll the pipeline up to one reporting currency. Live on every tier.
items.lead: Quote a Monterrey customer in pesos and a Windsor customer in Canadian dollars, and still see one pipeline number in US dollars on Monday morning.
items.answer: Multi-currency in KanchanFlow lets each quote, order and invoice carry its own currency with an exchange rate locked at the moment of pricing, while the RFQ-to-Order CRM rolls every open deal up to a single reporting currency. The locked rate means your margin does not move between quoting and invoicing without somebody deciding it should.
summary: USA manufacturers rarely sell only in dollars. Cross-border work into Canada and Mexico, a European OEM's purchasing office, an Indian contract customer — each expects to be quoted in a currency they can approve internally. Doing that in a spreadsheet means the rate is whatever the person remembered on the day.

We attach the currency and the rate to the document. The quote is priced at a rate you locked, the order inherits it, and the invoice uses it unless you deliberately re-rate. Reporting converts everything to your base currency using those document rates, so pipeline and revenue figures are traceable back to individual deals.

capabilities.title: Currency per document
capabilities.body: Quotes, orders and invoices each carry their own currency. A customer who buys in euros and a customer who buys in dollars sit in the same pipeline without either being converted at report time only.

capabilities.title: Rate locked at pricing
capabilities.body: The exchange rate is captured onto the quote when you price it. It does not float. If you want to re-rate, that is an explicit action on a new revision that the customer can see.

capabilities.title: Base currency roll-up
capabilities.body: Pipeline value, booked orders and outstanding receivables all report in your base currency using the rate on each document, so the total is a sum of real deals rather than a re-conversion.

capabilities.title: Customer default currency
capabilities.body: Set the currency once on the customer and every new quote for them starts in it. Fewer decisions per quote means fewer quotes sent in the wrong currency.

capabilities.title: Forecasting in one currency
capabilities.body: Sales forecasts convert at document rates so a weakening currency shows up as a smaller forecast rather than being hidden by a re-conversion at today's rate.

howItWorks.text: Choose the currency all reporting rolls up to. For a USA shop that is US dollars; it is set once at the workspace level.

howItWorks.name: Set a default currency per customer
howItWorks.text: On the customer record, choose the currency they buy in. New quotes for that customer open in it automatically.

howItWorks.name: Price the quote and lock the rate
howItWorks.text: Enter line prices in the quote currency. The rate against your base currency is captured on the quote at that moment and shown on the header.

howItWorks.name: Convert to an order
howItWorks.text: The order inherits the currency and the locked rate from the accepted revision, so the value you booked is the value you quoted.

howItWorks.name: Invoice and report
howItWorks.text: The invoice uses the order's currency and rate. Aging, pipeline and forecast views convert with the document rates so every total traces back to specific records.

faqs.q: Does the rate update after I send the quote?
faqs.a: No. It is locked to the document. Re-rating is an explicit action that creates a new revision, so the customer sees the change rather than discovering it on the invoice.

faqs.q: Can one customer have quotes in two currencies?

faqs.q: How does this affect the pipeline number?

items.name: US tax rates
items.h1: US tax rates and SaaS jurisdictions
items.metaDescription: Apply the right US sales tax rate by jurisdiction on invoices, including states that tax software and services differently. Live on every tier.
items.lead: State, county and local rates applied by ship-to jurisdiction, with resale and manufacturing exemption certificates recorded against the customer.
items.answer: US tax rates in KanchanFlow apply state, county and local sales tax by ship-to jurisdiction on every invoice raised in the RFQ-to-Order CRM, including the states that treat software and services differently from goods. Exemption certificates sit on the customer record, so an exempt manufacturer is not taxed by accident.
summary: American sales tax is not one rate. It is a state rate plus county and municipal rates that depend on where the goods are delivered, and a taxability question that depends on what you sold. A machined part, a repair service and a software subscription can all be treated differently in the same state.

We hold the jurisdiction rate tables and the SaaS taxability treatment, and apply them from the ship-to address on the document. Where the customer holds a resale or manufacturing exemption certificate, that certificate is on their record with an expiry date, and the invoice reflects it rather than relying on somebody remembering.

capabilities.title: Jurisdiction rates by ship-to address
capabilities.body: State, county and local components are resolved from the delivery address on the document, not from the customer's billing address, which is where most manual calculations go wrong.

capabilities.title: SaaS and service taxability
capabilities.body: Software subscriptions and services are treated according to the destination state's rules rather than being taxed like goods by default. The states that diverge are the states that generate the audit letters.

capabilities.title: Exemption certificates on the customer
capabilities.body: Record a resale or manufacturing exemption certificate with its number and expiry. Invoices to that customer apply the exemption, and an expired certificate flags rather than silently continuing.

capabilities.title: Line-level tax treatment
capabilities.body: A single invoice can carry a taxable line and an exempt line. Freight, tooling and services often differ from the parts they accompany, and the invoice shows each line's treatment.

capabilities.title: Tax detail on the printed document
capabilities.body: The invoice shows the jurisdiction breakdown rather than one lumped tax figure, which is what a customer's accounts payable team checks against their own system.

howItWorks.name: Enter the ship-to address
howItWorks.text: The delivery address on the quote or order is the input to the tax calculation. Different ship-to addresses on the same customer are handled separately.

howItWorks.name: Resolve the jurisdiction
howItWorks.text: The address maps to a state, county and local jurisdiction set, and the applicable rates for each are pulled from the rate tables.

howItWorks.name: Apply the taxability rule
howItWorks.text: Each line is treated according to what it is — goods, service or software — in that destination state. Lines are not assumed to share a treatment.

howItWorks.name: Check for an exemption
howItWorks.text: If the customer holds a valid, unexpired resale or manufacturing exemption certificate, the exemption applies and the certificate reference is stored against the invoice.

howItWorks.name: Show the breakdown
howItWorks.text: The invoice prints the jurisdiction components and the total tax, so the customer's AP team can reconcile it without calling you.

tierAvailability.professional: Included on every tier.

faqs.a: No. Nexus is a legal determination for you and your tax adviser. We apply rates and taxability to documents once you tell us where you are registered to collect.

faqs.q: How are exemption certificates handled at expiry?
faqs.a: The certificate carries an expiry date. Once it passes, the exemption stops applying and the customer record flags it, so you chase the renewal rather than absorbing an assessment.

faqs.q: Can freight be taxed differently from the parts?
faqs.a: Yes. Taxability is decided per line, which matters because freight and tooling are treated differently from goods in several states.

faqs.q: Do you file sales tax returns?
faqs.a: No. We produce correct invoices and the underlying detail. Filing happens through your accountant or a filing service.

faqs.q: Is this included on Starter?
faqs.a: Yes. US tax rates, like the India regulatory suite, are on every tier. We do not charge more for getting the tax on your invoice right.

items.name: WhatsApp Business Hub
items.h1: WhatsApp Business Hub — inbox, flows, calls, templates, broadcasts
items.metaTitle: WhatsApp Business Hub — shared inbox and flows
items.metaDescription: A shared WhatsApp inbox on the official Business API with template messages, flows, broadcasts and calls, tied to the customer and quote records. Live today.
items.lead: Buyers chase quotes on WhatsApp whether or not your CRM knows about it. This puts that conversation on the customer record, on the official API, with a shared inbox the whole desk can see.
items.answer: The KanchanFlow WhatsApp Business Hub runs your shop's WhatsApp on the official Business API as a shared inbox inside the RFQ-to-Order CRM. Every message, template, flow, broadcast and call attaches to the customer, quote or order it concerns, so a follow-up thread is not trapped on one salesperson's personal phone.
summary: In manufacturing sales the real conversation moved to WhatsApp years ago. Drawings arrive there, revised quantities arrive there, and 'when can you ship' arrives there at nine at night. The problem is not the channel; it is that the channel lives on a personal handset and leaves the business when that person does.

We connect a WABA number to the workspace so messages land in a shared inbox and thread against the right customer. Templates cover the repeatable sends — quote issued, quote expiring, dispatch notification. Broadcasts handle price-list and shutdown announcements. Calls and their recordings sit on the same record as the messages.

capabilities.title: Shared inbox on the official Business API
capabilities.body: Conversations belong to the company, not a phone. Assign a thread, hand it over during leave, and read the history when the customer references something from six months ago.

capabilities.title: Threads bound to customers, quotes and orders
capabilities.body: A message from a known number attaches to that customer record. Reply from inside a quote and the thread is linked to that quote, so context is not reconstructed from memory.

capabilities.title: Template messages for repeatable sends

capabilities.title: Flows for structured replies
capabilities.body: Send a short structured flow to collect a quantity, a delivery date preference or a drawing revision, and write the answer straight back onto the record rather than into prose you have to read.

capabilities.title: Broadcasts to segmented lists
capabilities.body: Send a price revision or a plant shutdown notice to a filtered customer or dealer list. Delivery and read counts come back against the broadcast.

capabilities.title: Calls and recordings on the record
capabilities.body: WhatsApp calls initiated from the hub are logged against the customer with duration, and recording where you have enabled it, alongside the message history.

items.name: IndiaMART lead capture
items.metaDescription: Pull IndiaMART enquiries into the CRM automatically, de-duplicate against existing accounts and route them to an owner within minutes. Live on every tier.
items.lead: Enquiries stop sitting in a portal inbox until someone logs in. They arrive as leads, de-duplicated and assigned, with the product enquired about already attached.
items.answer: IndiaMART auto lead capture pulls enquiries from your IndiaMART seller account into KanchanFlow within minutes, de-duplicates them against existing accounts, and routes each to an owner. Because the RFQ-to-Order CRM treats an enquiry as the start of an RFQ, the lead arrives with the product enquired about already attached.
summary: IndiaMART generates volume, and volume decays fast. A buyer who sends the same enquiry to six suppliers usually engages with whoever replies first. If your enquiries sit in a portal inbox until someone remembers to check it, you are competing on a delay you chose. Response speed is the one variable on that enquiry you fully control.

The connector polls your seller account and creates a lead for each new enquiry, carrying the buyer's name, company, phone, city and the product line they asked about. Repeat enquiries from a number or company already in the system attach to the existing account instead of creating a duplicate, and assignment follows the rules you set.

capabilities.title: Automatic enquiry pull

capabilities.title: De-duplication against existing accounts

capabilities.body: The product or category the buyer enquired about lands on the lead, so the salesperson opens the record already knowing what the conversation is about.

capabilities.title: Owner assignment on arrival

capabilities.title: Straight into WhatsApp follow-up

items.name: Mobile app
items.metaDescription: A native iOS and Android app for quoting, approvals, customer lookup and field visits, built for a phone used with gloves on a shop floor. Live on every tier.
items.lead: Built for the people who are not at a desk: the owner approving a discount from a customer's lobby, the salesperson logging a visit in a parking lot, the plant manager checking an order from the floor.
items.answer: The KanchanFlow mobile app is a native iOS and Android client for the RFQ-to-Order CRM, not a shrunken web page. It covers customer lookup, quote review and approval, order status, visit check-in and WhatsApp follow-up, with large touch targets and offline-tolerant behaviour for shops with poor coverage.
summary: Manufacturing sales does not happen at a desk. The estimator is on the floor with the print, the owner is in a customer's lobby, and the field salesperson is in a truck between two plants. A CRM that only works properly on a laptop gets updated at nine at night, if at all, and usually from memory.

The app carries the parts of the workflow that genuinely need to be mobile. Look up a customer and their open quotes before you walk in. Approve a discount that is sitting on your name. Check in at a visit and dictate what happened. Reply to a buyer on WhatsApp from the record rather than from your personal thread.

capabilities.title: Customer and quote lookup
capabilities.body: Search a customer, see their open quotes, last order, outstanding balance and recent conversation before you walk into the meeting. Nothing about that should require a laptop.

capabilities.title: Approvals on the phone
capabilities.body: Discount and margin approvals that are waiting on you appear as a list with the numbers that matter — quoted price, cost, resulting margin — and approve or reject in two taps.

capabilities.title: Visit check-in with GPS
capabilities.body: Check in at a customer site and the visit is logged with location and time. The record is created where the visit happened, not reconstructed on Friday.

capabilities.title: Order and dispatch status
capabilities.body: Look up an order and see what has shipped, what is outstanding and what has been invoiced, so you can answer the question standing in front of you.

capabilities.title: Built for a shop-floor phone
capabilities.body: Large touch targets, high contrast, and screens that stay usable with gloves and in daylight. It tolerates intermittent connectivity rather than throwing an error and losing your input.

howItWorks.name: Install and sign in
howItWorks.text: Download from the App Store or Google Play and sign in with your workspace credentials. Your permissions and role home screen come with you.

howItWorks.name: Start from your home screen
howItWorks.text: The app opens on the role-specific home screen — an owner sees approvals and the command centre summary, a salesperson sees today's visits and open quotes.

howItWorks.name: Work the record in front of you
howItWorks.text: Search a customer, open a quote, check an order. Actions taken on the phone write to the same records as the web app immediately.

howItWorks.name: Log the field work
howItWorks.text: Check in at a visit, capture what was discussed, photograph a part or a drawing, and attach it to the customer without emailing it to yourself.

howItWorks.name: Follow up from the record
howItWorks.text: Call or message the buyer from inside the record so the activity is logged against the account rather than living on your personal phone.

tierAvailability.starter: Included. Two role-specific home screens — Owner and Salesperson.
tierAvailability.professional: Included. All eight role-specific home screens.
tierAvailability.enterprise: Included. All eight home screens plus custom role-based access control.

faqs.q: Is it a native app or a wrapped website?
faqs.a: Native, for both iOS and Android. That matters for camera access, GPS check-in and behaving sensibly when the signal drops inside a steel building.

faqs.q: Does it work without a connection?
faqs.a: It tolerates intermittent connectivity — recently viewed records stay readable and input you have typed is not thrown away when the signal drops. It is not a fully offline system.

faqs.q: Can I build a quote from the phone?
faqs.a: You can review, revise pricing on and approve quotes from the phone. Building a complex multi-line quote from scratch is still better on a laptop, and we would rather say so.

faqs.q: Is the app an extra charge?
faqs.a: No. It is included on every tier and every seat. Starter gets two role home screens; Professional and Enterprise get all eight.

faqs.q: Does GPS run in the background?
faqs.a: No. Location is captured when a user checks in at a visit. We do not track staff location continuously, and we would not build that.

items.name: Field visits
items.h1: Field visits with GPS check-in and territory
items.metaDescription: Plan customer visits, check in with GPS at the site, capture what happened, and see coverage by territory. Live in KanchanFlow on every tier.
items.lead: A visit plan for the week, a check-in at the gate, notes captured while the conversation is fresh, and an honest coverage picture at the end of the month.
items.answer: Field visits in KanchanFlow plan, verify and record customer site visits inside the RFQ-to-Order CRM. A visit is checked in with GPS at the customer's location, notes and photographs attach to the account, and coverage reports show which accounts in a territory have actually been seen this quarter.
summary: Field sales in manufacturing is expensive. A day out is fuel, tolls and eight hours of a senior person's time, and the return on it is invisible if the only record is a line in an expense claim. The common failure is not dishonesty, it is that visits get written up days later from memory, or not at all.

We make the visit a record with a location and a time on it. The salesperson plans the week's calls, checks in when they arrive, captures what was discussed while it is fresh, and photographs the part or drawing that came up. At the end of the month you can see coverage by territory rather than by anecdote.

capabilities.title: Visit planning
capabilities.body: Plan the week's calls against accounts and see them on the mobile home screen each morning. Planned versus actual is visible, which is a more useful conversation than a headcount of visits.

capabilities.title: GPS check-in at the site
capabilities.body: Check in when you arrive. Location and time are captured at that moment against the customer, so the visit record is evidence rather than recollection.

capabilities.title: Notes and photographs on the account
capabilities.body: Capture what was discussed and photograph the part, the drawing on the table, or the competitor's product on the shelf. It attaches to the customer, not to a phone gallery.

capabilities.title: Territory coverage reporting
capabilities.body: See which accounts in a territory have been visited and which have not been touched in ninety days. Flat list on Starter, seven-level hierarchy on Professional and above.

capabilities.title: Follow-up actions from the visit
capabilities.body: Create the quote, the sample request or the callback directly from the visit record so the outcome is linked to the call that produced it.

howItWorks.name: Plan the week
howItWorks.text: Select accounts to visit and schedule them. The plan appears on the mobile home screen, ordered for the day.

howItWorks.name: Check in on arrival
howItWorks.text: Open the visit on the phone and check in. Location and timestamp are recorded against the customer record.

howItWorks.name: Capture while it is fresh
howItWorks.text: Type or dictate what was discussed, add photographs of parts or prints, and note the next step before leaving the car park.

howItWorks.name: Create the follow-up
howItWorks.text: Raise the quote, the sample request or the callback task straight from the visit so nothing depends on remembering it later.

howItWorks.name: Review coverage
howItWorks.text: At month end, look at coverage by territory and by account tier. The question is not how many visits happened but which accounts were left alone.

tierAvailability.professional: Included. Seven-level territory hierarchy with coverage reporting.
tierAvailability.enterprise: Included. Seven-level hierarchy plus custom territory structures.

faqs.q: Do you track salespeople all day?
faqs.a: No. Location is captured at check-in and nowhere else. Continuous tracking is a different product and a different relationship with your team, and we do not build it.

faqs.q: What if there is no signal at the customer's plant?
faqs.a: Check in and capture notes anyway. The record syncs when the connection returns, with the original check-in time preserved.

faqs.q: Can I see which accounts have not been visited?
faqs.a: Yes. Coverage reporting lists accounts with no visit in a period you choose, by territory. That list is usually more useful than the visit count.

faqs.q: Is territory hierarchy available on Starter?
faqs.a: Starter has a flat territory list. The seven-level hierarchy is on Professional and Enterprise, where the number of accounts makes the structure worth having.

faqs.q: Can a visit create a quote?
faqs.a: Yes. Raise the quote from the visit record and the two stay linked, so you can see which visits actually turned into quoted work.

items.name: Material tracking
items.metaDescription: Track customer-supplied and job-allocated material against an order, with receipt, consumption and return on the record the customer sees. Live today.
items.lead: Know what material arrived for which job, what has been consumed, and what is left to return — without a spreadsheet that only one person understands.
items.answer: Material tracking in KanchanFlow records the material tied to a customer order: what was received, what has been consumed, and what remains. Because it lives in the RFQ-to-Order CRM next to the quote and the order, the person answering the customer's question can see the material position without walking to the stores.
summary: Job shops handle material that is not theirs. Free-issue bar stock from the customer, castings shipped in for machining, a tooling blank held between orders — all of it needs to be accounted for, and most of it is tracked on a clipboard or in one person's spreadsheet. That works until the customer asks for a figure on a Tuesday afternoon.

We attach material to the order it belongs to. Receipt is recorded with quantity, heat or lot reference and the date it arrived. Consumption is recorded as the job runs, and the balance is what remains. When the customer asks how much of their material you are still holding, the answer is on the record they can already see the order on.

capabilities.title: Material receipt against an order
capabilities.body: Record what arrived, in what quantity, with the heat number, lot or certificate reference and the date. Customer-supplied material is separated from material you bought for the job.

capabilities.title: Consumption and scrap recorded as it happens
capabilities.body: Log consumption against the order as parts are made, including scrap. The remaining balance is a running figure rather than a stocktake surprise.

capabilities.title: Certificates attached to the lot
capabilities.body: Mill certs and test reports attach to the received material, so the traceability document is with the material record when the customer asks for it two years later.

capabilities.title: Return and disposal tracking
capabilities.body: Record material returned to the customer or scrapped with their agreement, so the closing balance on a job is zero for a reason you can point at.

capabilities.title: Visible on the order
capabilities.body: The material position appears on the order the salesperson is already looking at, which is where the customer's question arrives.

howItWorks.name: Open the order
howItWorks.text: Material is tracked against the customer order it belongs to, so it inherits the customer, the part and the job context without re-entry.

howItWorks.name: Record receipt
howItWorks.text: Enter quantity received, heat or lot reference, supplier or customer as the source, and the date. Attach the mill certificate or test report.

howItWorks.name: Log consumption
howItWorks.text: As the job runs, record material consumed and scrapped against the order. The balance updates on the order header.

howItWorks.name: Answer the customer from the record
howItWorks.text: When the buyer asks how much of their free-issue stock remains, the figure is on the order rather than in the stores manager's head.

howItWorks.name: Close the balance
howItWorks.text: Return or scrap the remainder with a record of what was agreed, and the job closes with a material balance of zero rather than an open question.

tierAvailability.starter: Included. Manual milestone and material updates.
tierAvailability.professional: Included. Material milestones can be updated from an ERP webhook.
tierAvailability.enterprise: Included. Multi-plant material positions roll up across entities.

faqs.q: Does this replace our inventory system?
faqs.a: No. We track material against a specific customer order. Stock levels, reorder points and purchasing belong in an inventory system or ERP, and we say so plainly.

faqs.q: Can I track customer free-issue material separately?
faqs.a: Yes. Material is marked by source, so customer-supplied stock is distinguished from material you bought for the job, which is what matters when you reconcile at the end.

faqs.q: Where do mill certificates live?
faqs.a: Attached to the received lot on the order. When a customer asks for traceability on a shipment from two years ago, the certificate is on the record, not in a filing cabinet.

faqs.q: Can I see material across several orders for one customer?
faqs.a: Yes, from the customer record. Enterprise rolls this up across plants where you run more than one site.

faqs.q: Does consumption update automatically from the shop floor?
faqs.a: Only where you feed it from an ERP webhook on Professional or Enterprise. Otherwise it is recorded by a person, and we do not pretend otherwise.

items.name: AI agent with approval mode
items.h1: AI agent with human approval before send
items.metaDescription: AI agents draft the RFQ extraction and the follow-up message, then wait for a human to approve before anything is sent. Approval-first on every tier.
secondaryKeywords: human in the loop ai sales
items.lead: The agent drafts. A person approves. Nothing reaches a customer because a model decided it should — and every run costs a known number of credits.
items.answer: KanchanFlow's AI agents draft work inside the RFQ-to-Order CRM and stop for human approval before anything leaves the building. The RFQ Agent turns an emailed enquiry into a structured RFQ; the Quote Follow-Up Agent drafts the chase message. Both are approval-first by default, and every run costs a published number of credits.
summary: The reason shops distrust AI in sales software is not accuracy, it is autonomy. A model that emails a customer on its own will eventually email the wrong customer the wrong price, and you will find out from the customer. We built the approval step in as the default rather than as a setting most people never find.

Two agents are on every tier: RFQ extraction, which reads an enquiry email and produces a structured RFQ with parts, quantities and dates for you to check; and Quote Follow-Up, which drafts the chase message in your tone with the quote reference and the outstanding decision. Professional adds seven more, and Enterprise adds custom prompts.

capabilities.title: Approval before send, by default
capabilities.body: Drafted messages sit in a review queue with the customer, the quote and the exact text. Approve, edit or discard. Nothing is dispatched on the agent's own judgement.

capabilities.title: RFQ extraction from an email
capabilities.body: An enquiry email becomes a structured RFQ with part numbers, quantities, materials and required dates, each field showing what it was extracted from so you can check it against the original.

capabilities.title: Quote follow-up drafting
capabilities.body: The follow-up draft references the quote number, the revision, what is outstanding and when it expires, so the chase reads like a person who knows the deal wrote it.

capabilities.title: Published credit weights
capabilities.body: An RFQ email extract costs two credits, a follow-up draft costs one, a page of OCR costs three. Every operation has a published weight so the bill is predictable.

capabilities.title: Extraction shown next to the source
capabilities.body: Each extracted field is shown against the text it came from. Checking an agent's work should take fifteen seconds, not a re-read of the whole email.

howItWorks.name: The trigger happens
howItWorks.text: An enquiry email arrives, or a quote passes its follow-up date. The relevant agent picks it up automatically.

howItWorks.name: The agent drafts
howItWorks.text: The RFQ Agent produces a structured RFQ; the Follow-Up Agent produces a message. Credits are deducted at the published weight for that operation.

howItWorks.name: A human reviews
howItWorks.text: The draft appears in the review queue with its source material alongside. You approve, edit before approving, or discard it.

howItWorks.name: Approved work is applied
howItWorks.text: An approved RFQ is created as a record; an approved message is sent through the chosen channel and logged on the customer timeline.

howItWorks.name: Usage is visible
howItWorks.text: Credit consumption is reported per agent and per user, so you can see what the AI is actually costing before the month ends.

tierAvailability.starter: 2 basic agents — RFQ Agent and Quote Follow-Up. 100 AI credits per paid user per month.
tierAvailability.professional: All 9 agents. 500 AI credits per paid user per month, plus vector search via credits.
tierAvailability.enterprise: All 9 agents plus custom agent prompts. Committed credit pool with fair use.

faqs.q: Can the AI send a message without me?
faqs.a: Not by default, and that default is the feature. Drafts wait in a review queue for a person to approve. We would rather be slower than surprise you in front of a customer.

faqs.q: What does a run cost?
faqs.a: Every operation has a published credit weight — two credits for an RFQ email extract, one for a follow-up draft, three per page of OCR. Starter includes 100 credits per user per month, Professional 500.

faqs.q: Which agents are on Starter?
faqs.a: Two: the RFQ Agent and Quote Follow-Up. Professional includes all nine, adding quote risk, reorder prediction, dealer health and forecasting.

faqs.q: How do I check an extraction quickly?
faqs.a: Each extracted field is displayed against the source text it came from, so verifying a ten-line RFQ is a scan rather than a re-read.

faqs.q: Do you train models on our data?
faqs.a: No. Your quotes, drawings and customer data are not used to train models. Agents run against your records to do your work, and that is the end of it.

items.name: Manufacturing workspace
items.h1: Manufacturing workspace — dashboard, customers, inventory, orders, purchase orders, shipments
items.metaDescription: One workspace covering dashboard, customers, inventory view, orders, purchase orders and shipments, laid out for how a job shop actually works. Live today.
items.lead: Not a generic CRM with 'Deals' renamed. The navigation is customers, orders, purchase orders and shipments, and the home screen changes depending on whose it is.
items.answer: The manufacturing workspace is the shell of the KanchanFlow RFQ-to-Order CRM: a role-specific dashboard plus customers, inventory view, orders, purchase orders and shipments. It is organised around the documents a job shop actually passes around rather than around a generic opportunity pipeline borrowed from software sales.
summary: Most CRMs are built for a sales motion where the object of interest is a deal and the deliverable is a signature. In a job shop the objects are an RFQ, a drawing revision, a quote, a customer PO, a dispatch note and an invoice — and the person using the system is as likely to be a plant manager as a salesperson.

The workspace reflects that. The navigation names the real documents. The home screen is role-specific, so an owner opens on approvals and the command centre while an estimator opens on RFQs waiting to be priced. Starter has two of those home screens, Professional has all eight, Enterprise adds custom role-based access control.

capabilities.title: Role-specific home screens
capabilities.body: Owner, salesperson, estimator, inside sales, plant manager, dealer manager, finance and administrator each open on the work waiting for them rather than on a generic dashboard everyone ignores.

capabilities.title: Customers with plants and contacts
capabilities.body: A customer is a company with plants, contacts and buying history, not a single row. Professional adds plant records and stakeholder mapping; Enterprise adds multi-entity roll-up.

capabilities.title: Orders, purchase orders and shipments
capabilities.body: The customer order, the customer's purchase order document, and what actually shipped are three separate things and are treated as three separate things.

capabilities.title: Inventory view
capabilities.body: A read of what is on hand and allocated for the orders you are quoting and running. It answers 'can we promise this date', not 'what should we buy'.

capabilities.title: Manufacturing templates by vertical
capabilities.body: Pre-built field sets and stages for common shop types. Five verticals on Starter, twelve on Professional, twelve plus custom on Enterprise.

capabilities.title: Search across documents
capabilities.body: Search a part number and get the RFQs, quotes, orders and shipments it appears on. Most questions in a shop start with a part number, not a company name.

howItWorks.name: Pick your vertical template
howItWorks.text: Choose the template closest to your shop — machining, fabrication, contract assembly and so on. It sets sensible stages, fields and home screens rather than an empty system.

howItWorks.name: Assign roles
howItWorks.text: Give each user a role. The role sets their home screen and their permissions, so the estimator does not open on a dealer dashboard.

howItWorks.name: Bring in customers and contacts
howItWorks.text: Import your account list with plants and contacts, or let the lead connectors populate it. Duplicate detection runs on import.

howItWorks.name: Work the documents
howItWorks.text: RFQ to quote to order to dispatch to invoice, each as its own record with links back to the one before it.

howItWorks.name: Watch it from the dashboard
howItWorks.text: The owner command centre and the revenue leakage dashboard read the same records, so the numbers on the wall match the records underneath them.

tierAvailability.professional: 8 role home screens, 12 vertical templates, unlimited contacts and accounts, 100 GB storage.
tierAvailability.enterprise: 8 home screens plus custom RBAC, 12 templates plus custom, unlimited records, 500 GB or more storage.

faqs.q: Is this an ERP?
faqs.a: No. It manages customer RFQs, quotes, follow-ups and order handoff. Routing, capacity, BOM explosion and shop-floor scheduling belong in an ERP or MRP system, and we do not claim to replace one.

faqs.q: How many role home screens do I get?
faqs.a: Two on Starter — Owner and Salesperson. All eight on Professional. Enterprise adds custom role-based access control on top of the eight.

faqs.q: What are the vertical templates?
faqs.a: Pre-built stage and field configurations for common shop types, so you start with something recognisable rather than an empty CRM. Five on Starter, twelve on Professional and Enterprise.

faqs.q: Can I search by part number?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is the search we optimised for. A part number returns the RFQs, quotes, orders and shipments it appears on across every customer.

faqs.q: What does the inventory view actually do?
faqs.a: It shows what is on hand and allocated so you can answer a delivery promise. It does not run reorder points, purchase planning or stock valuation.

items.name: Channel partner management
items.metaDescription: Manage dealers and channel partners with their own records, order history and portal access, so channel business stops living in an inbox. Live today.
items.lead: Dealers are not customers and not salespeople. They get their own records, their own order history, and on Professional their own portal to place and track orders.
items.answer: Channel partner management in KanchanFlow gives dealers and distributors first-class records inside the RFQ-to-Order CRM, separate from direct customers. Each partner carries its own order history, pricing and contacts, and on Professional a portal where the dealer places and tracks orders without going through your inside sales desk.
summary: Manufacturers who sell through a channel usually run it out of one manager's inbox and a spreadsheet of dealer codes. That works until the manager is on leave, or until you want to know which dealers have stopped ordering, or which ones are quoting against each other on the same end customer.

We model the dealer as its own record with contacts, agreed pricing, credit terms and complete order history. Starter carries twenty-five basic dealer records for shops with a small channel. Professional makes dealer counts unlimited, adds a five-level hierarchy for distributor and sub-dealer structures, and opens the dealer portal. Enterprise adds custom structures on top of the same five levels.

capabilities.title: Dealer records separate from customers
capabilities.body: A dealer buys to resell and needs different pricing, different credit terms and different reporting from a direct account. Mixing the two in one list is how channel reporting becomes useless.

capabilities.title: Five-level hierarchy
capabilities.body: Master distributor, regional distributor, dealer, sub-dealer and retail. Roll performance up or drill down, on Professional and Enterprise.

capabilities.title: Dealer portal
capabilities.body: Partners log in to place orders, see their order status, download invoices and check their outstanding balance without emailing your inside sales desk for each one.

capabilities.title: Partner-specific pricing
capabilities.body: Hold agreed dealer pricing and discount structures against the partner record so orders price correctly without a manual lookup on every line.

capabilities.title: Order history and reorder patterns
capabilities.body: Every dealer's ordering history is on the record, which is what the reorder prediction agent reads when it flags a partner who has gone quiet.

howItWorks.name: Create the partner record
howItWorks.text: Set up the dealer with contacts, addresses, agreed pricing, credit terms and their place in the hierarchy.

howItWorks.name: Set pricing and terms
howItWorks.text: Attach the dealer price list or discount structure. Orders from that partner price against it rather than against your direct list price.

howItWorks.name: Give portal access
howItWorks.text: On Professional and Enterprise, invite the partner's contacts to the portal so they can place and track orders themselves.

howItWorks.name: Take and fulfil orders
howItWorks.text: Dealer orders run through the same order, dispatch and invoice flow as direct business, with the dealer as the billing party.

howItWorks.name: Review channel performance
howItWorks.text: Look at ordering patterns by partner and by level of the hierarchy, and act on partners whose volume has dropped.

tierAvailability.starter: 25 basic dealer records. No hierarchy and no dealer portal.
tierAvailability.professional: Unlimited dealers, 5-level hierarchy and the dealer portal.
tierAvailability.enterprise: Unlimited dealers, 5-level hierarchy plus custom structures, dealer portal included.
