troubleshooting.cause: The template is pending review, was rejected, or was edited after approval, which resets it to pending.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the template's status in the template manager and read Meta's rejection reason. Rejections are usually promotional wording in a utility-category template.

troubleshooting.error: Messages stop sending after a spike in volume
troubleshooting.cause: The number hit its Meta messaging limit tier, which starts low and increases with good-quality sending history.
troubleshooting.fix: Wait for the 24-hour window to roll, reduce send volume, and improve quality rating. Limits raise automatically as your sending history matures; there is no way to buy your way up.

troubleshooting.error: Customer replies are not appearing in the CRM
troubleshooting.cause: The webhook subscription for messages was not enabled on the WhatsApp Business Account, or the callback verification failed.
troubleshooting.fix: Re-run the webhook setup from the connector page. Inbound messages received during the gap are not recoverable, which is why this should be verified during setup.

troubleshooting.error: Template quality rating dropped to low
troubleshooting.cause: Recipients blocked or reported the messages, usually because the template reads as marketing rather than a genuine transaction update.
troubleshooting.fix: Pause that template, rewrite it to reference the specific quote and part, and resubmit. Do not send marketing content from a number you rely on for quote delivery.

troubleshooting.error: Overage charges higher than expected
troubleshooting.cause: Each 24-hour conversation window is billed by Meta by category, and a burst of follow-ups opened many separate windows.
troubleshooting.fix: Review the usage panel by category. Consolidating follow-ups into fewer conversations reduces cost more than shortening individual messages does.

faqs.q: How is WhatsApp billed?
faqs.a: Every tier includes messages: 500 a month on Starter, 5,000 on Professional and 25,000 on Enterprise. Beyond that you pay Meta's own conversation cost plus our markup, which is 20 per cent on Starter, 15 on Professional and 10 on Enterprise. The full worked example is on the WhatsApp billing page at /whatsapp-billing.

faqs.q: Why is there a markup at all?
faqs.a: It covers the messaging infrastructure, template management and delivery monitoring we run on top of Meta's API. We publish the exact percentage at /whatsapp-billing rather than folding an invisible margin into the seat price.

faqs.q: Can I use my existing WhatsApp Business app number?
faqs.a: Yes, but migrating it to the Business API deletes the chat history on that number permanently. Most shops take a new number instead and keep the old one running for a transition month.

faqs.q: Do customers know they are talking to a business account?
faqs.a: Yes. The number shows your verified business display name, and the message experience is visibly a business one. That is a feature, not a drawback.

faqs.q: How many numbers can I have?
faqs.a: Starter includes one and can add two more at $25 each per month. Professional includes three and can add seven. Enterprise is unlimited.

faqs.q: Does the AI follow-up agent send messages on its own?
faqs.a: It drafts them. A person approves the send unless you explicitly turn on unattended sending for a specific template, which we recommend only for order-confirmation and dispatch notices.

items.tiers: All tiers — 500 / 5,000 / 25,000 messages included by tier; see /whatsapp-billing

items.name: IndiaMART Insta & Enquiries
items.tagline: Pull IndiaMART enquiries into the CRM within minutes, deduplicate them against existing accounts, and route them to an estimator.
items.metaDescription: IndiaMART integration for manufacturing CRM: pull Insta enquiries and buy leads into the RFQ pipeline with dedupe, routing and response tracking.
items.answer: KanchanFlow, the RFQ-to-Order CRM, pulls IndiaMART Insta enquiries and buy leads through the official CRM Integration API, deduplicates them against existing accounts, and routes each one to an estimator with a response clock running. Speed of first response is the single strongest predictor of conversion on this channel.
intro: IndiaMART leads decay faster than any other source we handle. The buyer has sent the same enquiry to five or six suppliers on the same afternoon, and the first credible reply usually takes the conversation. A lead sitting unread in a shared inbox for four hours is, in practice, a lost lead, and no amount of careful quoting afterwards recovers it.

The connector polls the enquiry API on a short cycle and creates a lead the moment one appears, matched against existing customers by phone and email so a repeat buyer does not become a duplicate account. Territory and product-line rules decide who owns it, and a visible response clock starts immediately.
items.frame: This connector is for USA manufacturers with India operations, India-based contract customers, or manufacturers exporting to India. IndiaMART is where Indian industrial buyers issue enquiries, so it matters if you supply into that market.

syncTo.detail: Where your IndiaMART account supports it, we mark an enquiry as actioned so it does not keep resurfacing in the seller panel after your estimator has picked it up.
Whether a first response was sent and when, written back so the seller panel and the CRM do not disagree about which enquiries are still open.
We deliberately do not push catalogue, pricing or product listing data to IndiaMART. Your listings stay managed in the IndiaMART panel by whoever owns them.
The IndiaMART enquiry ID is stored on our lead so a re-delivered enquiry updates the existing lead instead of creating a second one.

syncFrom.detail: Enquiry ID, date, subject, the product or category enquired about, and the enquiry type, whether Insta, buy lead or direct enquiry.
Name, company, mobile, alternate mobile, email and city, which is the whole contact set IndiaMART exposes.
The buyer's own words, preserved verbatim on the lead, because the phrasing is often the only clue to whether they want one part or a thousand.
Parsed into structured fields when IndiaMART supplies them, left in the message text when it does not.
City and state, used for territory routing and to work out whether the enquiry is inside your realistic delivery radius.

items.cadence: Every 5 minutes during Indian business hours, every 15 minutes otherwise

screenshots.caption: The lead inbox filtered to IndiaMART, showing enquiries with their response clocks, the matched existing account where one was found, and the assigned estimator.
screenshots.note: Capture with at least one clock in a warning state so the urgency is visible. Date stamp required.

screenshots.caption: A single IndiaMART lead expanded, showing the verbatim enquiry text, buyer contact block, and the Convert to RFQ action.
screenshots.note: Capture with buyer contact details masked in the product. Date stamp required.

screenshots.caption: The IndiaMART source report showing enquiries received, first-response median and conversion to quote over the last 90 days.
screenshots.note: Capture real figures from a workspace with genuine history, or omit the shot rather than fake numbers. Date stamp required.

setup: Log in to the IndiaMART seller panel with an account that has administrator rights on the listing.
Navigate to Lead Manager, then the CRM Integration section, and generate a CRM integration key for your mobile number.
Note the key exactly. IndiaMART keys are long and are frequently truncated when pasted from a phone message.
In KanchanFlow, open Settings, Integrations, IndiaMART and enter the key together with the registered mobile number on the IndiaMART account.
Run the connection test. It fetches the last 24 hours of enquiries read-only and shows you what it found without creating any leads.
Review the sample and confirm the field mapping, particularly which IndiaMART product category maps to which of your product lines.
Set the dedupe rule. Matching on mobile number is the default because IndiaMART buyers reuse numbers across enquiries far more than they reuse email addresses.
Configure routing. Territory by buyer state, product line by enquiry category, or round robin. Round robin is the honest default for shops with one estimator per shift.
Set the response-time target and the escalation. Thirty minutes to first response with escalation to the sales manager at sixty is what we see work.
Turn on the WhatsApp first-response template if the WABA connector is live, because the fastest credible reply on this channel is usually a WhatsApp message, not an email.
Enable live import and watch the first day's leads land before you rely on it.
limitations: IndiaMART's API is rate limited and their documented guidance is not to poll more often than every five minutes. We honour that, so a lead can be up to five minutes old when it reaches you.
The API exposes only the fields IndiaMART chooses to expose. Attachments a buyer uploaded in the IndiaMART panel do not come through, and there is no way for us to fetch them.
Historical backfill is limited to the window IndiaMART allows on the key, typically the last seven days. You cannot import years of past enquiries.

Lead quality on this channel is genuinely mixed. A meaningful share of enquiries are traders, resellers and price-shoppers rather than manufacturers, and no amount of routing logic changes that. Plan your estimator time accordingly.
We cannot post replies to a buyer through IndiaMART's own messaging. Responses go out by phone, email or WhatsApp from the CRM.

If the IndiaMART key is regenerated in their panel, our polling fails silently from their side until you re-enter it. We alert on consecutive empty responses, but the first hour can look like a quiet day rather than an outage.

troubleshooting.error: Connection test succeeds but no leads are ever imported
troubleshooting.cause: The key is scoped to a different mobile number than the one receiving enquiries, common where a business has several IndiaMART logins.
troubleshooting.fix: Regenerate the key from the account that actually owns the listing, and confirm the mobile number in the connector matches that account.

troubleshooting.error: Every enquiry creates a new account instead of matching the existing one
troubleshooting.cause: Dedupe is set to email matching and IndiaMART buyers frequently submit with different email addresses.
troubleshooting.fix: Switch dedupe to mobile number as the primary key with email as a secondary. Then merge the duplicates already created from the account list.

troubleshooting.error: Leads arrive with the message text truncated
troubleshooting.cause: The buyer's enquiry exceeded the length IndiaMART returns through the API.
troubleshooting.fix: Open the enquiry in the IndiaMART panel for the full text. We show the truncation marker rather than silently presenting a partial message as complete.

troubleshooting.error: Import stopped after a burst of enquiries
troubleshooting.cause: The API rate limit was hit, usually because a manual re-sync was run alongside the scheduled poll.
troubleshooting.fix: Wait for the next cycle. Do not run repeated manual syncs; they consume the same quota the scheduled poll needs.

troubleshooting.error: Duplicate leads appear for one enquiry
troubleshooting.cause: IndiaMART re-delivered the enquiry with a new ID after the buyer edited it.
troubleshooting.fix: Merge the leads and set the fuzzy dedupe window to one hour, which catches re-delivered enquiries from the same number about the same product.

faqs.q: How quickly do leads reach the CRM?
faqs.a: Within five minutes during Indian business hours. That is the fastest IndiaMART's own rate guidance permits and we do not pretend otherwise.

faqs.q: Which tiers include IndiaMART?
faqs.a: Starter includes one selectable lead source, so you can choose IndiaMART. Professional and Enterprise include unlimited lead sources. An extra source on Starter is $10 per month.

faqs.q: Can I reply through IndiaMART from the CRM?
faqs.a: No. IndiaMART does not expose outbound messaging to integrators. Replies go out as WhatsApp, email or a phone call logged against the lead.

faqs.q: Does it import old enquiries?
faqs.a: Only the short window IndiaMART allows on the key, usually seven days. There is no full historical backfill and we will not claim one.

faqs.q: Do I still need the IndiaMART panel?
faqs.a: Yes, for catalogue and listing management. We handle enquiries, not your storefront.

faqs.q: Is IndiaMART worth it for a USA shop?
faqs.a: Only if you supply Indian buyers or run an India entity. If your customers are all domestic USA, choose Meta Lead Ads or your website forms as your lead source instead.

items.tiers: All tiers — Starter includes one selectable lead source; Professional and Enterprise include unlimited

items.name: JustDial
items.tagline: Capture JustDial leads into the RFQ pipeline with the call recording reference, so a phone enquiry becomes a tracked lead.
items.metaDescription: JustDial integration for manufacturing CRM: capture JustDial leads and call enquiries into your pipeline with dedupe, routing and response-time tracking.
items.answer: KanchanFlow, the RFQ-to-Order CRM, receives JustDial leads over their webhook so a phone or app enquiry lands in the pipeline within seconds, with the caller's number, the searched category and the JustDial lead reference. Leads deduplicate against existing accounts by mobile number before anyone is assigned.
intro: JustDial is a phone-first channel. A buyer searches a category, JustDial connects the call, and a lead reference is generated whether or not anybody in your shop picked up. That last part matters: the missed calls are as informative as the answered ones and they usually go unrecorded.

The connector takes the webhook JustDial sends and turns it into a lead with the category searched, the caller's number and the reference, deduplicated against your existing accounts. Missed enquiries are visible as leads with no first response, which is generally the first uncomfortable report a shop runs after switching this on.
items.frame: This connector is for USA manufacturers with India operations, India-based contract customers, or manufacturers exporting to India. JustDial is an Indian local-search channel and is of no use outside that market.

syncTo.detail: Where the JustDial account supports acknowledgement, we confirm receipt so the lead is not re-sent repeatedly to the same webhook.
We do not manage your JustDial listing, catalogue, photos or paid campaign settings, and we do not write anything back into the JustDial panel.
The JustDial lead reference is stored on our lead so a redelivered webhook updates the existing record rather than creating a second one.

syncFrom.detail: The JustDial lead ID and the moment the enquiry was generated, which is the clock the response target runs against.
The buyer's mobile and the name JustDial holds, which is the primary dedupe key against existing accounts.
What the buyer searched for and which of your JustDial listings they reached, used for product-line routing.
Whether the connected call was answered or missed, which is what makes the missed-enquiry report possible.
Used for territory routing and for judging whether the enquiry is inside your delivery radius.

items.cadence: Real time by webhook; a 15-minute reconciliation poll catches anything the webhook missed

screenshots.caption: The lead inbox filtered to JustDial, showing answered and missed enquiries side by side with their response clocks.
screenshots.note: Capture with genuine missed enquiries present. Date stamp required; mask caller numbers in the product.

screenshots.caption: A JustDial lead expanded showing the searched category, the call outcome flag and the Convert to RFQ action.
screenshots.note: Capture from a live workspace. Date stamp required.

screenshots.caption: The missed-enquiry report for the last 30 days with counts by day of week and hour.
screenshots.note: Capture real data. If the workspace has none, do not stage the shot. Date stamp required.

setup: Log in to the JustDial seller dashboard with an account that administers the listing.
Open the lead settings and locate the API or webhook integration section. On some account types this must be enabled by JustDial support first.
In KanchanFlow, open Settings, Integrations, JustDial and copy the webhook URL and secret shown there.
Paste both into the JustDial dashboard as the lead delivery destination.
Ask JustDial support to send a test lead, or generate one by calling your listed number from a phone that is not already in your CRM.
Confirm the test lead appears in the CRM lead inbox with the correct category and number.
Set the dedupe rule to mobile number. JustDial provides no email, so mobile is the only reliable key.
Configure routing by search category so a sheet-metal enquiry does not land with the machining estimator.
Set the response target. JustDial callers are usually still comparing suppliers within the hour, so fifteen to thirty minutes is the realistic window.
Turn on the missed-enquiry alert so an unanswered connected call raises a task rather than disappearing.
Watch a full day of live leads before relying on the routing rules.
limitations: JustDial supplies a mobile number, a name and a category. There is no enquiry text, no quantity, no drawing and no email, so every lead needs a human call to qualify it.
Webhook delivery is not guaranteed and JustDial does not offer a replay facility. Our reconciliation poll narrows the gap but cannot fully close it.

Lead quality is the weakest of any channel we integrate. A large share of JustDial enquiries for industrial categories are individuals, brokers or wrong-category clicks, and the connector cannot filter them for you.
No historical backfill exists. From the day you connect it forward, and nothing before.
Some JustDial account tiers do not expose webhook delivery at all, and whether yours does is a commercial matter between you and JustDial.
We cannot attribute a lead to a specific paid campaign, so return on JustDial spend cannot be measured inside the CRM beyond raw lead counts and conversion.

troubleshooting.error: No leads arrive after setup
troubleshooting.cause: Webhook delivery is not enabled on that JustDial account tier, or the URL was saved without the secret.
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm with JustDial support that lead API delivery is active for your listing, then re-copy both the URL and the secret from the connector page.

troubleshooting.error: Leads arrive with a blank category
troubleshooting.cause: The enquiry came through a JustDial channel that does not carry category data, such as some app-based callbacks.
troubleshooting.fix: Set a default routing rule for uncategorised leads so they land with a named person rather than sitting unassigned.

troubleshooting.error: The same caller creates a new lead every time they ring
troubleshooting.cause: Dedupe is off or the number arrives in different formats, sometimes with the country code and sometimes without.
troubleshooting.fix: Enable mobile dedupe with number normalisation in connector settings, which strips the country code before matching.

troubleshooting.error: Webhook signature verification failures in the log
troubleshooting.cause: The secret in JustDial's dashboard does not match the connector, usually after the secret was rotated on one side.
troubleshooting.fix: Rotate the secret from the connector page and paste the new value into JustDial. Rotating in JustDial alone will not work.

troubleshooting.error: Response clock shows leads as breached immediately
troubleshooting.cause: The timestamp JustDial sends is in Indian Standard Time and the workspace timezone is set to US Eastern.
troubleshooting.fix: Set the workspace timezone correctly in Settings, General. The connector converts, but only once it knows the target timezone.

faqs.q: Does it capture missed calls?
faqs.a: Yes, where JustDial flags the call outcome. Missed enquiries create leads with no first response, which is usually the most useful report a shop gets from this connector in its first week.

faqs.q: Which tiers include JustDial?
faqs.a: Starter includes one selectable lead source. Professional and Enterprise include unlimited sources. An extra source on Starter is $10 per month.

faqs.q: Is there any enquiry text?
faqs.a: No. JustDial passes a number, a name and a category. Everything else has to come from the call your estimator makes.

faqs.q: Can I see which JustDial campaign a lead came from?
faqs.a: No. Campaign attribution is not exposed to integrators, so return on spend has to be judged from lead volume and conversion rather than campaign level detail.

faqs.q: Should a USA-only shop use this?
faqs.a: No. JustDial is an Indian local-search channel with no relevance to a domestic USA customer base. Leave it off.

faqs.q: What happens to leads if the webhook fails?
faqs.a: The reconciliation poll picks up what it can, but JustDial has no replay mechanism, so a prolonged outage means genuinely lost leads. That is a property of the channel and worth knowing before you rely on it.

items.tiers: All tiers — Starter includes one selectable lead source; Professional and Enterprise include unlimited

items.name: TradeIndia
items.tagline: Import TradeIndia buy leads and enquiries into the RFQ pipeline, including the export enquiries that matter to overseas suppliers.
items.metaDescription: TradeIndia integration for manufacturing CRM: import buy leads and enquiries, including export enquiries, with dedupe, routing and response tracking.
items.answer: KanchanFlow, the RFQ-to-Order CRM, imports TradeIndia buy leads and direct enquiries through their lead API, deduplicates them against existing accounts and routes them by product category. TradeIndia carries a higher proportion of export and bulk enquiries than the other Indian directories, which changes how you should qualify them.
intro: TradeIndia sits somewhere between a directory and a marketplace. Its buy leads are usually posted by buyers looking for bulk or export supply, which means the enquiries carry more quantity information than a JustDial callback and more commercial intent than a general category search. They also go to more suppliers at once, so speed still decides who gets the conversation.

The connector polls the lead API, creates a lead per enquiry with the buy-lead text intact, and routes on product category. Because a meaningful share of these are export enquiries, the connector flags leads with a non-Indian destination so they can go to whoever handles documentation rather than into the domestic queue.
items.frame: This connector is for USA manufacturers with India operations, India-based contract customers, or manufacturers exporting to India. It is also the channel where an India entity finds export enquiries from third countries.

syncTo.detail: We mark a lead as retrieved so it does not resurface on every poll in the TradeIndia panel.
Product listings, catalogue content and paid membership settings remain managed in the TradeIndia seller panel.
The TradeIndia enquiry ID is stored on our lead, so a re-delivered enquiry updates rather than duplicates.

syncFrom.detail: The buyer's posted requirement in full, which on TradeIndia usually names a quantity, a specification and sometimes a target price.
Company name, contact person, phone, email and country. The country field is what drives our export flag.
Used for routing to the right estimator and product line.
Parsed where TradeIndia provides them as structured fields, preserved in the text where it does not.
Whether the record is a posted buy lead, a direct product enquiry or a catalogue enquiry, because each converts at a different rate.

items.cadence: Every 15 minutes, or on demand from the connector page

screenshots.caption: The lead inbox filtered to TradeIndia, with the export flag visible on leads from non-Indian buyers.
screenshots.note: Capture with at least one genuine export-flagged lead. Date stamp required; mask buyer contact details in the product.

screenshots.caption: A TradeIndia buy lead expanded showing the full posted requirement text, parsed quantity and the Convert to RFQ action.
screenshots.note: Capture a lead that genuinely carries a quantity so the parsing is visible. Date stamp required.

screenshots.caption: The connector settings page showing category-to-product-line mapping with several categories mapped.
screenshots.note: Capture from a configured workspace, not an empty mapping table. Date stamp required.

setup: Log in to the TradeIndia seller panel with an administrator account for the listing.
Open the lead management section and generate API credentials. TradeIndia issues a user ID and a profile-specific key.
Note whether your membership tier includes API lead access. Free listings generally do not.
In KanchanFlow, open Settings, Integrations, TradeIndia and enter the user ID and key.
Run the connection test, which reads recent leads without creating anything, and inspect the sample.
Map TradeIndia categories to your product lines. Leave anything you do not make unmapped so it routes to a review queue rather than an estimator.
Set the dedupe rule. Email plus mobile works better here than on the other Indian directories because TradeIndia buyers are more often businesses with stable contact details.
Turn on the export flag rule so leads with a non-Indian country route to whoever owns export documentation.
Set the response target. Buy leads are less time-critical than IndiaMART enquiries; four business hours is a realistic first-response target.
Enable live import and review the first week's leads for category mapping gaps.
limitations: API lead access depends on your TradeIndia membership tier. If your plan does not include it, this connector cannot work and that is a commercial matter with TradeIndia, not a technical one.
Buy leads are broadcast to many suppliers simultaneously. A lead reaching you is not a lead that is yours, and conversion on this channel is correspondingly low.
Attachments and specification documents posted with a buy lead are not exposed through the API. You have to open the panel for those.
Quantity parsing is best-effort. Free-text requirements such as one container load or as per drawing cannot be turned into a number, and we leave them as text rather than guessing.
Historical backfill is limited to the window TradeIndia's API exposes, typically a few days.
Export flags rely on the country field being populated by the buyer. Buyers frequently leave it blank, so the flag catches most but not all export enquiries.

troubleshooting.error: Authentication fails with an invalid profile ID
troubleshooting.cause: The key was generated against a different seller profile than the one you entered.
troubleshooting.fix: Regenerate the key from the correct profile in the TradeIndia panel and re-enter both the user ID and the key together.

troubleshooting.error: Leads import but all route to the review queue
troubleshooting.cause: No category mappings have been configured, which is the safe default.
troubleshooting.fix: Open the connector's category mapping table and map your active categories. Leave genuinely irrelevant categories unmapped on purpose.

troubleshooting.error: Quantity field is empty on leads that clearly state a quantity
troubleshooting.cause: The quantity is inside the free-text requirement rather than in a structured field.
troubleshooting.fix: Read the requirement text on the lead. We do not infer a numeric quantity from prose because a wrong quantity on an RFQ is worse than no quantity.

troubleshooting.error: Import returns nothing despite leads visible in the panel
troubleshooting.cause: The membership tier does not include API access, or the API entitlement lapsed with a renewal.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the entitlement with TradeIndia. The connector reports zero leads rather than an error because the API answers successfully with an empty set.

troubleshooting.error: Same buyer creates several accounts
troubleshooting.cause: The buyer posts from different email addresses across enquiries.
troubleshooting.fix: Set dedupe to mobile-primary with email as secondary, then merge the existing duplicates from the account list.

faqs.q: How is TradeIndia different from IndiaMART?
faqs.a: TradeIndia buy leads carry more quantity and specification detail and a higher share of export enquiries, but volume is lower and each lead is broadcast to more suppliers. Neither is a substitute for the other.

faqs.q: Which tiers include TradeIndia?
faqs.a: Starter includes one selectable lead source. Professional and Enterprise include unlimited sources. An extra source on Starter is $10 per month.

faqs.q: Do buy-lead attachments come through?
faqs.a: No. TradeIndia does not expose them through the API, so specification files still need to be pulled from the seller panel by hand.

faqs.q: Can I reply from the CRM?
faqs.a: Not through TradeIndia's own messaging. Replies go out by email, phone or WhatsApp and are logged against the lead.

faqs.q: Why is conversion so low on this channel?
faqs.a: Because a posted buy lead goes to many suppliers at once. Treat it as a prospecting list rather than an inbound enquiry, and measure it accordingly.

faqs.q: Is it useful to a USA-only shop?
faqs.a: Only if you are pursuing export business into or out of India. A domestic USA shop should spend that lead-source slot on Meta Lead Ads or website forms.

items.tiers: All tiers — Starter includes one selectable lead source; Professional and Enterprise include unlimited

items.name: Meta Lead Ads
items.tagline: Pull Facebook and Instagram lead form submissions into the pipeline in seconds, with campaign, ad set and ad recorded against every lead.
items.metaDescription: Meta Lead Ads integration for manufacturing CRM: instant Facebook and Instagram lead capture with campaign attribution, dedupe and routing.
items.answer: KanchanFlow, the RFQ-to-Order CRM, subscribes to Meta's leadgen webhook so a Facebook or Instagram lead form submission reaches an estimator within seconds, carrying campaign, ad set and ad names. That attribution is what lets a shop see which ad produced quoted revenue rather than which produced form fills.
intro: Manufacturers who advertise on Meta usually measure the wrong thing, because the ad platform can only report the form fill. Whether that lead became an RFQ, a quote, or an order is invisible on the Meta side, so budget decisions get made on cost per lead rather than cost per quoted dollar.

This connector carries the campaign, ad set and ad identifiers through to the lead, then keeps them attached as the lead becomes an RFQ, a quote and an order. The source report then shows spend against quoted and won value, which is the only version of this report worth looking at.

syncTo.detail: We register a leadgen webhook subscription against each page you select, which is the only object we create on the Meta side.
Each leadgen ID is retrieved and acknowledged so Meta does not keep redelivering a lead we have already stored.
The Meta leadgen ID is stored against our lead, so a webhook redelivery updates the existing record rather than creating a second one.
We do not create, edit, pause or budget campaigns, and we do not upload conversion events. This connector reads leads and nothing else, which is why we do not request ads management scope.

syncFrom.detail: Every field on the form, including custom questions, mapped to CRM fields you choose. Unmapped answers are preserved on the lead rather than discarded.
Names and IDs for all three levels, which is what makes downstream attribution possible.
Whether the lead came from Facebook or Instagram and in which placement, useful because the two convert very differently for industrial offers.
The moment the form was submitted, which the response clock runs from rather than from the moment we received it.
Instagram and Facebook page forms can generate leads without ad spend; we mark which is which so cost per lead is not miscalculated.

items.cadence: Real time by webhook, typically within seconds; a 15-minute poll backfills any missed submission

screenshots.caption: The lead inbox filtered to Meta Lead Ads, showing campaign and ad names on each lead card alongside the response clock.
screenshots.note: Capture from a workspace with a genuinely running campaign. Date stamp required; mask lead contact details in the product.

screenshots.caption: The field mapping screen showing Meta form questions on the left mapped to CRM fields on the right, including one unmapped custom question.
screenshots.note: Capture with a real multi-question form. Date stamp required.

screenshots.caption: The source attribution report showing spend, leads, quotes issued and quoted value by campaign.
screenshots.note: Requires real campaign data; do not fabricate spend figures. Date stamp required and recapture each quarter.

setup: Confirm you are an admin on the Meta Business Manager account that owns the Facebook page and the ad account.
In KanchanFlow, open Settings, Integrations, Meta Lead Ads and click Connect.
Authorise on Meta's own consent screen. We request leads retrieval, pages read engagement and ads read. Read the scopes; we do not ask for ads management.
Select the pages whose lead forms you want to import. A page not selected here sends nothing.

Map the fields for each active lead form. Full name, email, phone and company are usually straightforward; custom questions such as material or annual volume need a decision about which CRM field they belong in.
Decide what happens to unmapped answers. The default is to keep them on the lead as a note, which is better than losing them.
Set the dedupe rule. Email primary with phone secondary suits Meta leads, because the form usually pre-fills a real email from the user's profile.
Configure routing by campaign or by a form field such as material type, so leads reach the estimator who can qualify them.
Set an aggressive response target. Meta leads go cold faster than most people expect; fifteen minutes is a reasonable target during business hours.
Submit a test lead using Meta's Lead Ads Testing Tool and confirm it appears in the CRM with campaign attribution.
Check the connector again after any new campaign launch, because a new form needs its fields mapping before its leads are useful.
limitations: Meta access tokens expire and the connection needs re-authorising periodically. A page admin change or a password reset can also invalidate it, and leads submitted while the connection is broken are recoverable only within Meta's own retention window.
A new lead form's custom questions arrive unmapped. Leads still import, but the answers sit as notes until someone maps them, which is easy to forget in the week a campaign launches.

Lead quality on Meta for industrial offers is highly variable and the form's low friction is exactly why. Expect a substantial share of unqualified submissions and design your qualification step around it.
We do not push conversion events back to Meta, so the ad platform cannot optimise against your quoted or won value. Attribution is visible in our reports only.
We cannot retrieve leads submitted before the connector was authorised beyond Meta's retention window.
Instagram lead forms expose fewer placement details than Facebook ones, so placement-level analysis is thinner on the Instagram side.

troubleshooting.error: Leads stopped arriving with no error shown
troubleshooting.cause: The Meta access token expired or was invalidated by a page role change.
troubleshooting.fix: Reconnect from the connector page. Set a calendar reminder to check the connection quarterly; the connector also emails the workspace owner when the token nears expiry.

troubleshooting.error: Leads arrive with no campaign name
troubleshooting.cause: The lead came from an organic page form rather than a paid ad.
troubleshooting.fix: Nothing is wrong. Filter on the organic flag in the source report so organic leads are not counted against ad spend.

troubleshooting.error: Custom question answers are missing from lead fields
troubleshooting.cause: The form is new and its questions have not been mapped.
troubleshooting.fix: Open field mapping for that form. The answers are already on the lead as notes and will be moved into fields for future submissions once mapped.

troubleshooting.error: Test lead does not appear
troubleshooting.cause: The page was not selected during setup, or the Lead Ads Testing Tool submitted against a form on a different page.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the page selection in connector settings and re-run the test against a form on a selected page.

troubleshooting.error: Duplicate leads from the same person
troubleshooting.cause: The same user submitted two different forms, which Meta treats as two distinct leads.
troubleshooting.fix: Enable cross-form dedupe on email in connector settings. Leave it off if you deliberately want to see repeat interest as separate signals.

faqs.q: How fast do leads arrive?
faqs.a: Usually within a few seconds of submission, because Meta pushes a webhook rather than us polling. The response clock runs from the submission time, not from our receipt.

faqs.q: Which tiers include Meta Lead Ads?
faqs.a: Starter includes one selectable lead source. Professional and Enterprise include unlimited. An extra source on Starter is $10 per month.

faqs.q: Can I see which ad produced revenue?
faqs.a: Yes. Campaign, ad set and ad stay attached through RFQ, quote and order, so the source report shows quoted and won value by ad, not just lead count.

faqs.q: Do you send conversions back to Meta?
faqs.a: No. We do not push conversion events to the ads platform, so Meta cannot optimise on your downstream outcomes. If that matters to you, say so before you buy rather than after.

faqs.q: Does it work with Instagram lead forms?
faqs.a: Yes, through the same connection. Instagram exposes less placement detail than Facebook, so reporting on that side is slightly thinner.

faqs.q: What happens if the connection breaks?
faqs.a: We alert the workspace owner and attempt backfill on reconnection, but leads outside Meta's retention window are genuinely lost. Check the connection quarterly.

items.tiers: All tiers — Starter includes one selectable lead source; Professional and Enterprise include unlimited

items.name: Google Forms
items.tagline: Turn an RFQ request form into structured leads, including the drawing file the customer uploaded, without anyone watching a spreadsheet.
items.metaDescription: Google Forms integration for manufacturing CRM: convert RFQ request form responses into leads with file uploads, field mapping, dedupe and routing.
items.answer: KanchanFlow, the RFQ-to-Order CRM, watches a Google Form's responses and creates a lead or an RFQ for each submission, carrying uploaded drawings and specification files across as attachments. It is the cheapest way to put a real RFQ request form on a shop's website without building anything.
intro: Plenty of shops already have a quote request form built in Google Forms, usually because somebody needed one on a Friday afternoon and it was the fastest thing available. It works perfectly well as a form. The problem is what happens next: the responses sit in a spreadsheet that somebody is supposed to check, and on a busy week nobody does.

This connector keeps the form and removes the spreadsheet watching. Each response becomes a lead, or directly an RFQ if you map it that way, with the file upload question turned into a real attachment on the record. The estimator gets the drawing without downloading it from Drive and re-uploading it.

syncTo.detail: We register a watch against the selected form so new responses are picked up, which is the only object we create in your Google account.
For each mapped file upload answer we request that specific file from Drive by ID, and nothing else in the account is read.
The Google response ID is stored against the lead so a replayed response updates rather than duplicating the record.
We never edit the form, add or reorder questions, change its settings, or write anything to the linked response spreadsheet.

syncFrom.detail: Every question on the form, mapped to CRM fields you choose. Short answer, paragraph, multiple choice, checkbox, dropdown, date and linear scale are all supported.
Files uploaded through the form's file question are fetched from Drive and attached to the lead or RFQ, which is the part that makes this connector worth having.
Where the form collects it, used as the primary dedupe key and as the reply-to for the acknowledgement.
The response time, which the response clock runs from.

items.cadence: Every 5 minutes; a manual Sync now is available on the connector page

screenshots.caption: The connector's form picker showing the available Google Forms in the connected account with response counts.
screenshots.note: Capture the genuine picker. Date stamp required; form names may be blurred.

screenshots.caption: The field mapping screen with a file upload question mapped to RFQ attachments and a dropdown mapped to material.
screenshots.note: Capture with a real multi-question RFQ form. Date stamp required.

screenshots.caption: A resulting RFQ record showing the mapped fields and the customer's uploaded STEP file attached.
screenshots.note: Capture with a genuine CAD file attachment present, not a placeholder document. Date stamp required.

setup: Identify the Google account that owns the form. Ownership matters; edit access alone is not sufficient for the file upload path.
In KanchanFlow, open Settings, Integrations, Google Forms and click Connect.
Authorise with the owning Google account. We request read access to forms and read access to the specific Drive files uploaded through them.
Select the form to connect. One connector binding handles one form; connect several bindings if you run separate forms for RFQ and general enquiry.
Choose whether responses create a Lead or an RFQ directly. RFQ is right if your form asks for part, quantity and drawing; Lead is right for a general contact form.
Map each question to a CRM field. Take the time to map quantity and material properly, because those two drive routing and the RFQ Agent's first pass.
Map the file upload question to attachments. Without this, files stay in Drive and the estimator will not see them.

Set the dedupe rule to respondent email, and decide whether a repeat submission from the same email updates the existing lead or creates a new one. For RFQ forms, a new record is usually correct because it is a new job.
Configure routing by material or product line if the form asks, otherwise round robin.
Enable the acknowledgement email so the customer knows the request landed. Silence after submitting an RFQ form is the most common complaint buyers have about shops.
Submit a test response including a file upload and confirm the attachment arrives on the record.
limitations: The file upload question requires the respondent to be signed in to a Google account. Many industrial buyers are not, and they will hit a sign-in wall on your form. This is Google's behaviour and there is nothing we can do about it.
Uploaded files live in the form owner's Drive and count against that account's storage quota. If the quota fills, uploads fail at the form, not at our connector.
We poll every five minutes rather than receiving a push, so a response can be up to five minutes old when it reaches the CRM.

Changing a question's text in Google Forms breaks its mapping, because Google identifies questions by ID and a rewritten question is often a new ID. Responses still import; that field arrives unmapped until someone fixes it.
Google Forms offers no server-side validation you can rely on, so expect malformed phone numbers and quantities typed as words. We import what was submitted rather than silently correcting it.
There is no spam protection on a public Google Form. If your form URL gets scraped you will receive junk, and the only real remedy is moving to a form with a CAPTCHA.

troubleshooting.error: File upload question shows no attachment on the record
troubleshooting.cause: The mapping for that question is not set to attachments, or the connected Google account cannot read the uploaded file.
troubleshooting.fix: Set the mapping, then confirm the connected account is the form owner. Uploads are stored in the owner's Drive and a non-owner may lack access.

troubleshooting.error: A field stopped populating after the form was edited
troubleshooting.cause: The question was rewritten and Google issued a new question ID.
troubleshooting.fix: Reopen field mapping and re-map the question. The connector shows unmapped questions at the top of the list for exactly this reason.

troubleshooting.error: Responses stop importing entirely
troubleshooting.cause: The Google OAuth grant was revoked, or the form owner's account was suspended.
troubleshooting.fix: Reconnect from the connector page with the owning account. Responses submitted during the outage import on reconnection because they remain in the response sheet.

troubleshooting.error: Junk submissions flooding the lead inbox
troubleshooting.cause: The public form URL is being hit by a bot.
troubleshooting.fix: Restrict the form to signed-in users, or move to a form platform with CAPTCHA such as Typeform. We can filter on keywords but that is a poor substitute for real protection.

troubleshooting.error: Quantity imports as text and breaks RFQ creation
troubleshooting.cause: A respondent typed a quantity as words or with a unit inside the same field.
troubleshooting.fix: Change the form question to a short answer with number validation, and set the connector to route unparseable quantities to a review queue rather than failing the import.

faqs.q: Can responses become RFQs directly?
faqs.a: Yes. If your form asks for part, quantity and a drawing, map it to create an RFQ rather than a lead and it will arrive in the estimating queue ready to work.

faqs.q: Do customer drawings come across?
faqs.a: Yes, where the form has a file upload question and it is mapped to attachments. The respondent has to be signed in to a Google account for that question to work, which is Google's rule, not ours.

faqs.q: Which tiers include Google Forms?
faqs.a: Starter includes one selectable lead source. Professional and Enterprise include unlimited. An extra source on Starter is $10 per month.

faqs.q: How current is the data?
faqs.a: Within five minutes. Google Forms does not offer a push notification we can subscribe to, so we poll.

faqs.q: Can I connect more than one form?
faqs.a: Yes, one binding per form. Shops commonly run a general contact form and a detailed RFQ form with different mappings and different routing.

faqs.q: Is it good enough as a permanent RFQ intake?
faqs.a: It is good enough to start, and plenty of shops never move off it. If you need spam protection, conditional logic or upload from unauthenticated buyers, Typeform is the better fit.

items.tiers: All tiers — Starter includes one selectable lead source; Professional and Enterprise include unlimited

items.name: Typeform
items.tagline: Take a conditional RFQ intake form, complete with uploads and logic jumps, straight into the estimating queue.
items.metaDescription: Typeform integration for manufacturing CRM: instant webhook capture of RFQ intake forms with logic jumps, file uploads, hidden fields and UTM attribution.
items.answer: KanchanFlow, the RFQ-to-Order CRM, receives Typeform submissions by webhook within seconds, including file uploads, logic-jump answers and hidden fields carrying UTM parameters. It is the intake form we recommend when a shop wants a real qualification flow rather than a flat list of questions.
intro: A good RFQ intake form asks different questions depending on the answer before it. A sheet-metal enquiry needs material, gauge and finish; a machining enquiry needs tolerance, surface finish and whether material certification is required. Asking every buyer all of it every time is how you end up with a long form that people abandon halfway through.

Typeform handles that branching well, and this connector carries the result across intact. Answers arrive by webhook in seconds, hidden fields bring UTM parameters and referrer with them, and file uploads land as attachments on the RFQ so the estimator has the drawing in front of them straight away.

syncTo.detail: Where you connect the account rather than configuring by hand, we register the webhook against the selected form with a signing secret.
For each mapped file upload answer we fetch that specific file from Typeform's storage at submission time, so the attachment survives their retention window.
The Typeform response token is stored on the lead, so a webhook redelivery updates the existing record rather than duplicating it.
We never modify questions, logic jumps or settings, and we never write responses back into Typeform.

syncFrom.detail: Every answered question, with unanswered branches recorded as skipped rather than blank, which matters when you are auditing why a field is empty.
Drawings, specifications and photos uploaded through a file question, fetched and attached to the lead or RFQ.
UTM source, medium, campaign, referrer and any custom hidden field you pass in the form URL, preserved for attribution.
Whether the form was completed or partially submitted, and how long it took, which is a useful signal of enquiry seriousness.
Where you use Typeform's scoring logic to pre-qualify, the score arrives and can drive routing.

items.cadence: Real time by webhook; a 15-minute reconciliation poll backfills any missed submission

screenshots.caption: The connector setup page showing the Typeform webhook URL and secret alongside the connected form.
screenshots.note: Capture the genuine setup page. Date stamp required; the secret must be masked in the product.

screenshots.caption: Field mapping showing logic-branch questions mapped to CRM fields, with hidden UTM fields mapped to source attribution.
screenshots.note: Capture a real branching RFQ form. Date stamp required.

screenshots.caption: The resulting RFQ with the branch answers, the attached drawing and the campaign attribution visible in the source panel.
screenshots.note: Capture end to end from one genuine submission. Date stamp required; recapture each quarter.

setup: Build or identify the Typeform you want to connect. If you are starting fresh, ask for part description, quantity, material, tolerance, target date and a drawing upload as the minimum useful RFQ intake.

In KanchanFlow, open Settings, Integrations, Typeform and choose Connect account or Webhook only. Connecting the account lets us list your forms; webhook only works if you prefer not to grant account access.
Copy the webhook URL and signing secret from the connector page.
In Typeform, open the form, go to Connect, Webhooks, and add the endpoint with the secret. Enable it.
Send a test submission from Typeform's own webhook panel and confirm it arrives in the CRM.
Map each question to a CRM field. Typeform identifies questions by a stable reference, so set the reference on each question rather than relying on the question text.
Map the file upload question to attachments.
Map hidden fields to your source attribution fields, and make sure your website appends the UTM parameters to the form URL, otherwise the hidden fields arrive empty.
Decide whether submissions create a Lead or an RFQ, and set routing on material, product line or Typeform score.
Configure partial submission handling. Importing partials gives you a list of people who started an RFQ and stopped, which is often worth a phone call.
Set the response target and enable the acknowledgement email.
Run one complete real submission with a file before pointing your website at the form.
limitations: Typeform is a paid product for anything beyond a small monthly response allowance, and file upload questions require a higher plan. That cost is yours, not ours.

File uploads on Typeform's own storage have retention limits by plan. We fetch files at submission time so the attachment survives, but a file we failed to fetch during an outage may be gone by the time we retry.
Question references must be set deliberately. If you duplicate a form, Typeform generates new references and the mappings on the copy will not carry over.

Webhook redelivery from Typeform is limited. A prolonged outage on our side is covered by the reconciliation poll only where the account connection is authorised; webhook-only setups have no backfill path at all.
We do not support Typeform's payment questions, and a form using one will import the submission without payment status.
Partial submissions are only available where you enable them in Typeform, and they arrive without the answers the respondent never reached, which can look like data loss if nobody explains it.

troubleshooting.error: Webhook shows delivered in Typeform but nothing appears in the CRM
troubleshooting.cause: Signature verification failed, usually because the secret was regenerated on one side only.
troubleshooting.fix: Copy the secret from the connector page into Typeform again. We reject unverified webhooks rather than accepting unsigned data.

troubleshooting.error: Mappings broke after duplicating a form
troubleshooting.cause: The duplicate has new question references.
troubleshooting.fix: Set the question references on the duplicate to match the original, or re-map. Setting references deliberately when the form is built avoids this entirely.

troubleshooting.error: Hidden UTM fields arrive empty
troubleshooting.cause: The website is linking to the form URL without appending the parameters.
troubleshooting.fix: Append the hidden field parameters to the form URL in your site's links. Typeform does not infer them from the referrer.

troubleshooting.error: Drawing attachment missing on an otherwise complete RFQ
troubleshooting.cause: The file fetch failed at submission time, most often because the file exceeded our 25 MB attachment ceiling.
troubleshooting.fix: The lead shows a fetch-failed marker with the file name. Ask the customer to resend, or retrieve it from Typeform's results view within its retention window.

troubleshooting.error: Partial submissions cluttering the lead inbox
troubleshooting.cause: Partial import is on and most respondents abandon early.
troubleshooting.fix: Filter partials into their own queue rather than turning them off. A partial with a phone number is often worth a call; one with nothing but a first name is not.

faqs.q: Why choose Typeform over Google Forms?
faqs.a: Logic jumps, uploads from buyers who are not signed in to a Google account, spam protection, and hidden fields for attribution. Google Forms is free and adequate; Typeform is the better intake form if you are serious about qualification.

faqs.q: How fast do submissions arrive?
faqs.a: Seconds, because Typeform pushes a webhook. The response clock runs from the submission timestamp.

faqs.q: Which tiers include Typeform?
faqs.a: Starter includes one selectable lead source. Professional and Enterprise include unlimited. An extra source on Starter is $10 per month.

faqs.q: Do file uploads work?
faqs.a: Yes, subject to your Typeform plan including file upload questions and our 25 MB per-attachment ceiling.

faqs.q: Can I capture people who start but do not finish?
faqs.a: Yes, if you enable partial submissions in Typeform. Route them to a separate queue; they are a calling list, not RFQs.

faqs.q: Can I connect several forms?
faqs.a: Yes, one binding per form, each with its own mappings and routing rules.

items.tiers: All tiers — Starter includes one selectable lead source; Professional and Enterprise include unlimited

items.name: Sulekha
items.tagline: Capture Sulekha service and supplier enquiries into the pipeline so a local enquiry is not lost between an app notification and a callback.
items.metaDescription: Sulekha integration for manufacturing CRM: capture Sulekha enquiries into your lead pipeline with dedupe, routing and response-time tracking.
items.answer: KanchanFlow, the RFQ-to-Order CRM, receives Sulekha enquiries through their lead delivery webhook and creates a deduplicated lead with the requirement text, the buyer's number and the category searched. It is the narrowest of our Indian lead channels and suits shops selling locally rather than nationally.
intro: Sulekha is a local-intent channel. Its enquiries tend to come from buyers looking for a supplier within reach rather than from procurement teams running a national sourcing exercise. That makes them smaller, closer and quicker to close when they are genuine, and it also makes them easy to lose, because a local enquiry that is not answered today is answered by somebody else tomorrow.

The connector puts those enquiries in the same pipeline as everything else, with the same response clock and the same dedupe rules. The value is not sophistication; it is that a Sulekha enquiry stops being an app notification somebody meant to act on and becomes a lead with an owner.
items.frame: This connector is for USA manufacturers with India operations, India-based contract customers, or manufacturers exporting to India. Sulekha is a local Indian channel; it has no function for a domestic USA customer base.

syncTo.detail: Receipt is acknowledged so the same enquiry is not re-sent on the next delivery cycle.
Listing content, category selection and paid plan settings stay in the Sulekha business panel.
The Sulekha enquiry ID is stored on the lead to suppress redelivery duplicates.

syncFrom.detail: The buyer's stated requirement, which on Sulekha is usually short and needs a call to qualify.
The contact set Sulekha exposes; email is often absent.
The category searched and the buyer's locality, used for routing and for judging travel distance on a site-visit job.
The moment the enquiry was raised, which the response clock runs from.

items.cadence: Real time by webhook where your Sulekha plan supports it; otherwise every 15 minutes by poll

screenshots.caption: The lead inbox filtered to Sulekha, showing enquiries with locality and response clocks.
screenshots.note: Capture from a live workspace with numbers masked in the product. Date stamp required.

screenshots.caption: A Sulekha lead expanded showing the requirement text, locality and the Convert to RFQ action.
screenshots.note: Capture a genuine enquiry. Date stamp required.

screenshots.caption: The lead source comparison report showing Sulekha alongside the other lead channels by volume and conversion.
screenshots.note: Requires real comparative data; do not stage it. Date stamp required.

setup: Log in to the Sulekha business dashboard with an administrator account.
Confirm your plan includes lead API or webhook delivery. Several Sulekha plans deliver leads only to the app and SMS, in which case this connector cannot be used.
In KanchanFlow, open Settings, Integrations, Sulekha and copy the webhook URL and secret.
Provide both to Sulekha through their dashboard or, on some account types, through their support team.
Request a test enquiry and confirm it arrives in the lead inbox.
Set dedupe on mobile number with normalisation, because Sulekha numbers arrive inconsistently formatted.
Map Sulekha categories to your product lines, sending anything unmapped to a review queue.
Set routing by locality if you have territory owners, otherwise round robin.
Set a short response target. Local enquiries convert on speed more than on price.
Enable the WhatsApp first-response template if the WABA connector is configured.
Review a week of live leads before extending the routing rules.
limitations: Lead API delivery is not available on every Sulekha plan, and whether yours has it is a commercial question for Sulekha, not something we can enable.
Enquiry detail is thin. A short requirement line, a name, a number and a locality is all that arrives, so every lead needs a qualifying call.
There is no email address in most enquiries, so email nurture is not possible on this channel without asking for it on the call.

This is the lowest-volume and lowest-value channel of the twenty-six connectors we ship, and for most manufacturers it will not justify a paid lead-source slot. We would rather you knew that before enabling it.
No historical backfill. Leads flow from connection forward only.
No campaign or spend attribution is exposed, so return on Sulekha spend cannot be calculated inside the CRM.

troubleshooting.error: No leads arrive after providing the webhook
troubleshooting.cause: The plan does not include API delivery, or Sulekha support has not activated it on the account.
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm entitlement with Sulekha directly. Until they activate delivery there is nothing to configure on our side.

troubleshooting.error: Numbers arrive with inconsistent formatting and duplicate accounts appear
troubleshooting.cause: Sulekha passes numbers sometimes with and sometimes without the country code.
troubleshooting.fix: Enable number normalisation in the dedupe settings, then merge the duplicates already created.

troubleshooting.error: All leads land in the review queue
troubleshooting.cause: No category mappings are configured.
troubleshooting.fix: Map the categories you actually serve. Leave the rest unmapped so irrelevant enquiries stay visible as such.

troubleshooting.error: Response clock shows breaches on arrival
troubleshooting.cause: Workspace timezone is not set to the timezone Sulekha timestamps in.
troubleshooting.fix: Set the workspace timezone in Settings, General. The connector converts once it knows the target.

troubleshooting.error: Enquiry text is empty
troubleshooting.cause: The buyer used a one-tap callback request rather than typing a requirement.
troubleshooting.fix: Nothing to fix. Treat these as call-me requests and route them to whoever can ring back fastest.

faqs.q: Is Sulekha worth a lead source slot?
faqs.a: For most manufacturers, no. Volume is low and detail is thin. If you are on Starter with one selectable source, spend it on IndiaMART or Meta Lead Ads instead.

faqs.q: Which tiers include Sulekha?
faqs.a: Starter includes one selectable lead source. Professional and Enterprise include unlimited, which is the realistic place for a channel like this.

faqs.q: Does it give me an email address?
faqs.a: Usually not. Sulekha enquiries are mobile-first, so plan on a call as the first response.

faqs.q: Can I measure return on my Sulekha spend?
faqs.a: Only by lead volume and conversion. No campaign or cost data is exposed to integrators.

faqs.q: Does it work outside India?
faqs.a: No. Sulekha is an Indian local-search platform with no relevance to a USA-only customer base.

faqs.q: What happens if I outgrow it?
faqs.a: Turn it off. Nothing else in the CRM depends on it and existing leads stay where they are.

items.tiers: All tiers — Starter includes one selectable lead source; Professional and Enterprise include unlimited

items.name: Gmail two-way sync
items.tagline: Every RFQ email, drawing attachment and quote reply threads onto the right record without anyone forwarding anything.
items.metaDescription: Gmail integration for manufacturing CRM: two-way email sync, RFQ extraction from inbound mail, drawing attachments on the record, and send-as from the CRM.
items.answer: KanchanFlow, the RFQ-to-Order CRM, syncs Gmail in both directions so inbound RFQ emails and their drawing attachments land on the customer record and quotes send from the estimator's own address. The RFQ Agent can read a matched inbound email and draft a structured RFQ from it, which costs two AI credits.
intro: In most shops the RFQ arrives as an email with a drawing attached, and the entire quoting process starts in somebody's inbox. That is fine until the person is on holiday, or the customer replies to the wrong thread, or the drawing that was quoted against turns out to be revision B when the email chain also contains revision C.

Two-way sync moves the record out of the inbox without moving the work. Mail continues in Gmail, but every message with a matched customer address threads onto the account, the attachments attach to the RFQ, and outbound quotes send from the estimator's own address so the customer sees a person, not a no-reply.

syncTo.detail: Sent through the user's own Gmail account so it appears in their Sent folder and replies come back to them, with the quote PDF attached and the quote number in the subject.
Follow-up emails drafted in the CRM send as replies within the original thread, which is what keeps the customer's mail client showing one conversation rather than five.
Where you enable it, a Gmail label is applied to synced threads so someone working in the inbox can see which conversations the CRM is tracking.
Meeting invitations created from a CRM activity send through the user's Google account so they carry their identity and free-busy correctly.

syncFrom.detail: Any message from or to an address on a customer or lead record threads onto that record, with the body stored and searchable.
Drawings, purchase orders and specification documents attach to the record. PDF and image attachments can be pushed to OCR at three credits per page.
Whether a thread is awaiting a reply from you or from the customer, which drives the follow-up queue.
Hard bounces mark the contact address as invalid so nobody keeps sending quotes to a person who left the company.
Detected and used to defer automated follow-ups rather than sending three nudges to someone on leave.

items.cadence: Near real time via Gmail push notifications; a 15-minute poll reconciles anything missed

screenshots.caption: A customer record's activity timeline showing an inbound RFQ email with its drawing attachment and the outbound quote reply threaded beneath it.
screenshots.note: Capture from a live workspace with a genuine multi-message thread. Date stamp required; mask the customer domain in the product.

screenshots.caption: The RFQ Agent's extraction preview, showing the source email on the left and the structured RFQ fields it proposes on the right, with a credit cost shown.
screenshots.note: Capture a real extraction including at least one field the agent could not determine. Date stamp required.

screenshots.caption: The connector's privacy settings showing the sync scope options: matched contacts only, or full mailbox.
screenshots.note: Capture the genuine settings screen. Date stamp required.

setup: Decide your sync scope before you connect. Matched contacts only syncs mail to and from addresses already on a CRM record; full mailbox syncs everything and is far more invasive.

Discuss that choice with your team. Full mailbox sync means their personal correspondence in a work account becomes visible in a shared system, and that conversation is better held before switching it on than after.
In KanchanFlow, open Settings, Integrations, Gmail and click Connect. Each user connects their own account; there is no single admin connection that covers everyone.
Authorise on Google's consent screen. We request read and send scopes on the connected mailbox, and we show exactly which on the connector page.
Choose the sync scope you decided on in step one.
Set the historical import window. Thirty days is the default; a longer window takes longer to complete and rarely changes any decision.
Configure send-as. If your estimators send from a shared address such as quotes@, add it as a send-as alias in Gmail first, then select it in the connector.
Turn on attachment sync and set the size ceiling. Our per-attachment limit is 25 MB.
Enable OCR on attachments only where you want it, because it consumes three AI credits per page and a fifty-page specification is not free.
Enable the RFQ Agent extraction if you want inbound emails drafted into structured RFQs. It costs two credits per extraction and always requires human confirmation.
Set up thread labelling if your team lives in the inbox rather than the CRM.
Send one test quote to yourself and confirm it appears in both Gmail Sent and the CRM timeline.
limitations: Each user connects individually. There is no Google Workspace domain-wide delegation option, so a twelve-person sales team means twelve connections and twelve consent screens.
Full mailbox sync stores message bodies from the connected account in your workspace. That is a real privacy decision and, in some jurisdictions, one your employees must be told about.
Gmail applies API quotas per account. A very large historical import can be throttled and take hours, and there is no way to buy priority.
Attachments above 25 MB are not synced. The message still threads, with a marker naming the file that was skipped.
We do not sync drafts, chats, or messages in Spam and Trash.

If a user changes their Google password or their account has its OAuth grant revoked by an administrator, sync stops silently from Google's side until they reconnect. We alert the user, but mail received in the gap imports only if it is inside the historical window on reconnection.

troubleshooting.error: Emails from a known customer are not threading onto their record
troubleshooting.cause: The message came from an address not on the customer record, commonly a personal or a plant-specific address.
troubleshooting.fix: Add the address to the contact. You can also enable domain matching, which threads any address on the customer's email domain, at the cost of occasionally catching the wrong person.

troubleshooting.error: Sync stopped and the user saw no warning
troubleshooting.cause: The OAuth grant was revoked, usually by a Workspace administrator tightening third-party app access.
troubleshooting.fix: Have the administrator allow the app in the Workspace admin console, then have the user reconnect. This is the single most common Gmail support ticket we see.

troubleshooting.error: Attachment missing from an RFQ
troubleshooting.cause: The file exceeded the 25 MB ceiling or was a Drive link rather than a real attachment.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask the customer to send the file directly, or download it from Drive and attach it manually. We do not follow Drive links from email bodies.

troubleshooting.error: Duplicate quote emails in the customer's inbox
troubleshooting.cause: The quote was sent from both the CRM and Gmail directly by the estimator.
troubleshooting.fix: Send quotes from one place. Enabling thread labelling makes it obvious in Gmail which conversations the CRM is already handling.

troubleshooting.error: AI credits consumed faster than expected
troubleshooting.cause: Attachment OCR is enabled and a customer sent a long specification document.
troubleshooting.fix: Set OCR to manual trigger rather than automatic. Three credits per page adds up quickly on a fifty-page document, and most pages of a spec do not need extracting.

faqs.q: Do you read the whole mailbox?
faqs.a: Only if you choose full mailbox sync. The default is matched contacts only, which syncs mail to and from addresses already on a CRM record and nothing else. We recommend leaving it there.

faqs.q: Which tiers include Gmail sync?
faqs.a: All tiers. The AI extraction that reads an inbound email and drafts an RFQ consumes AI credits, and credit allowances differ by tier.

faqs.q: Do quotes send from my address or yours?
faqs.a: Yours. The email goes through your connected Gmail account, appears in your Sent folder, and replies come back to you.

faqs.q: Can we use a shared quotes@ address?
faqs.a: Yes, as a Gmail send-as alias. Add it in Gmail first, then select it in the connector so estimators can send from the shared identity.

faqs.q: What happens to email if we stop using the CRM?
faqs.a: Nothing. Your mail was always in Gmail; we synced a copy of matched threads. Cancelling removes our access and leaves your mailbox untouched.

faqs.q: Does the AI agent send email on its own?
faqs.a: No. It drafts. A person reads and sends. We do not ship unattended outbound email from an AI agent, and we do not intend to.

items.tiers: All tiers — AI extraction from email consumes AI credits, which vary by tier

items.name: Outlook / Microsoft 365
items.tagline: Two-way mail and calendar sync for shops on Microsoft 365, with shared mailbox support for a quotes address the whole team works from.
items.metaDescription: Outlook and Microsoft 365 integration for manufacturing CRM: two-way email and calendar sync, shared mailbox support, attachment capture and RFQ extraction.
items.answer: KanchanFlow, the RFQ-to-Order CRM, syncs Outlook and Microsoft 365 mail and calendar in both directions through Microsoft Graph, including shared mailboxes. A shared quotes address is the usual setup in a USA job shop, and it is the one meaningful capability this connector has that the Gmail one does not.
intro: Most USA manufacturers we speak to are on Microsoft 365, and most of them run a shared mailbox for quote requests. That shared mailbox is the real RFQ queue, and it usually has no owner, no status and no way of telling whether a request from Tuesday was ever answered.

This connector treats the shared mailbox as a first-class source. Messages arriving there create or thread onto records, attachments land on the RFQ, and the queue gains a response clock and an owner. Individual mailboxes sync too, so an estimator's own correspondence with a customer shows on the account.

syncTo.detail: Sent through the user's own mailbox or the shared quotes mailbox, so it lands in the correct Sent Items and replies return to the right place.
Follow-up messages send as replies in the original conversation, preserving the conversation ID Outlook uses for threading.
An Outlook category is applied to synced conversations where enabled, so a person working in Outlook can see what the CRM is tracking.
Meetings created from a CRM activity are written to the user's Microsoft 365 calendar with attendees and a Teams link where the account provides one.

syncFrom.detail: Mail to and from addresses on customer or lead records, in individual and shared mailboxes alike.
Drawings, POs and specifications attach to the record, subject to our 25 MB per-attachment ceiling. OCR is available at three credits per page.
Meetings involving CRM contacts appear on the account timeline, and free-busy is read for scheduling.
Non-delivery reports mark bad addresses so quotes stop going to a contact who has left.
Out-of-office detection defers automated follow-up rather than sending nudges into an empty office.

items.cadence: Near real time via Graph change notifications; a 15-minute poll reconciles anything missed

screenshots.caption: The shared quotes mailbox rendered as a CRM queue, with each message showing its matched customer, owner and response clock.
screenshots.note: Capture from a live workspace with a genuinely busy shared mailbox. Date stamp required; mask sender domains in the product.

screenshots.caption: The Microsoft consent screen showing the Graph permissions requested and whether admin consent is required.
screenshots.note: Capture the genuine Microsoft screen including the admin consent notice. Date stamp required.

screenshots.caption: An RFQ record showing a purchase order attachment captured from the shared mailbox and its OCR extraction result.
screenshots.note: Capture a real PO OCR result including a field the OCR flagged as uncertain. Date stamp required.

setup: Establish whether your Microsoft 365 tenant requires administrator consent for third-party applications. Most manufacturer tenants do, and if yours does, an individual user cannot complete the connection alone.
Have a Global Administrator or Application Administrator grant consent from the connector's admin consent link. The permissions requested are listed on that page before consent.
Decide the sync scope: matched contacts only, or full mailbox. Matched contacts only is the default and the right choice for most shops.
In KanchanFlow, open Settings, Integrations, Outlook and connect the individual mailboxes that need syncing. Each user authorises their own.
Add the shared mailbox separately using Connect shared mailbox. The connecting user must have Full Access permission on it in Exchange.
Assign an owner and a response target for the shared mailbox queue. Without an owner, a shared mailbox stays exactly as unaccountable as it was before.
Set the historical import window; thirty days is the default.
Configure send-as for the shared address so estimators can reply as quotes@ rather than from their personal address.
Enable attachment sync and set the OCR policy. Manual OCR triggering is cheaper than automatic and usually sufficient.
Enable calendar sync if you want site visits and customer meetings on the account timeline.
Send a test message into the shared mailbox from an external address and confirm it creates a queue item with the correct clock.
Review the shared mailbox queue after one week and set routing rules based on what actually arrived.
limitations: Admin consent is required on most tenants. If your IT department will not grant it, this connector cannot be used, and no workaround exists that we would be willing to describe.
Microsoft Graph applies throttling per mailbox and per tenant. Large historical imports and busy shared mailboxes can be throttled, which shows as delayed rather than failed sync.
Attachments above 25 MB are not synced. The message threads with a marker naming the skipped file.
We do not sync Teams chat messages, only calendar events and mail. A quote negotiated in a Teams chat leaves no CRM record.
Shared mailbox sync requires Full Access permission for the connecting user. If that user leaves the company, the shared mailbox connection breaks and must be re-established by someone else.
On-premises Exchange without a Microsoft 365 hybrid configuration is not supported. Graph is the only interface we implement.

troubleshooting.error: Connect fails with Need admin approval
troubleshooting.cause: The tenant requires administrator consent for third-party applications and it has not been granted.
troubleshooting.fix: Send the admin consent link from the connector page to your Microsoft 365 administrator. Individual users cannot bypass this and should not try.

troubleshooting.error: Shared mailbox connects but no mail appears
troubleshooting.cause: The connecting user has Send As but not Full Access on the mailbox.
troubleshooting.fix: Have an Exchange administrator grant Full Access, then reconnect the shared mailbox. Send As alone permits sending but not reading.

troubleshooting.error: Sync shows Throttled during business hours
troubleshooting.cause: Graph is rate-limiting the tenant, often because another application is consuming the same quota.
troubleshooting.fix: The queue drains automatically. If it persists, narrow the sync scope to matched contacts and reduce the historical window.

troubleshooting.error: Calendar events duplicate
troubleshooting.cause: Both the CRM and an Outlook add-in are creating events for the same activity.
troubleshooting.fix: Disable one. Running two systems that both write to a calendar always produces duplicates and no configuration prevents it.

troubleshooting.error: Shared mailbox stopped syncing after an employee left
troubleshooting.cause: The connection was authorised by that employee's account, which has been disabled.
troubleshooting.fix: Reconnect the shared mailbox with a current employee who has Full Access. Use a service account rather than a person's account if you can, so this does not recur.
