faqs.q: Does it support shared mailboxes?
faqs.a: Yes, and that is the main reason this connector exists for USA shops. A quotes@ mailbox becomes a queue with owners, clocks and routing.

faqs.q: Do we need admin consent?
faqs.a: On most Microsoft 365 tenants, yes. There is a consent link on the connector page to send to your administrator, listing the exact permissions requested.

faqs.q: Which tiers include Outlook sync?
faqs.a: All tiers. AI extraction and OCR from mail consume AI credits, and credit allowances differ by tier.

faqs.q: Does it work with on-premises Exchange?
faqs.a: Only in a hybrid configuration that exposes Microsoft Graph. Pure on-premises Exchange is not supported.

faqs.q: What about Teams messages?
faqs.a: Not synced. Calendar and mail only. If your customers negotiate in Teams chat, that history stays in Teams.

faqs.q: Can two people work the shared mailbox queue?
faqs.a: Yes. Items can be claimed, assigned and escalated, and the response clock is visible to everyone rather than living in one person's head.

items.tiers: All tiers — AI extraction and OCR from email consume AI credits, which vary by tier

items.name: Google Calendar
items.tagline: Put site visits, capability audits and quote review calls on the calendar from the record, with travel time and free-busy respected.
items.metaDescription: Google Calendar integration for manufacturing CRM: two-way event sync for site visits and quote reviews, free-busy checking, travel buffers and reminders.
items.answer: KanchanFlow, the RFQ-to-Order CRM, syncs Google Calendar in both directions so a site visit or quote review booked from a customer record appears on the right calendar with the right attendees. Free-busy is read before a slot is offered, and travel buffers can be added automatically for on-site work.
intro: Scheduling in a job shop is not just meetings. It is a capability audit at a customer's plant three hours away, a first-article review, a supplier visit, and the quote review call that has to happen before Friday. Those all need to land on someone's calendar with enough travel time around them to be real.

This connector makes the calendar an extension of the record. Book from the customer, and the event carries the RFQ number, the attendees and the address. Free-busy is checked first, so nobody offers a customer a slot that is already taken, and travel buffers stop a two-hour drive being booked as a fifteen-minute gap.

syncTo.detail: Title carries the activity type and the customer, the description carries the RFQ or quote number and a link back to the record, and the location carries the plant address from the customer file.
Internal owners and the customer contacts on the activity are invited, so the customer receives a real invitation rather than a note in an email body.
Where an activity is flagged as on-site, buffer events before and after are created using the drive-time estimate you set for that customer.
Reminder timings from the activity type, so a site visit warns the day before and a call warns fifteen minutes before.
Changing or cancelling the activity updates or withdraws the calendar event rather than leaving an orphan on everyone's calendar.

syncFrom.field: Event changes made in Google Calendar
syncFrom.detail: Time changes, attendee responses and cancellations made in the calendar flow back to the activity, because most people reschedule from their calendar, not from the CRM.
Read for the users you are scheduling, so the slot picker only offers times that are genuinely open.
Accepted, declined or tentative per attendee, shown on the activity so a declined customer invitation is visible before the day.
Where a calendar event includes a known customer contact, it can be linked to that account automatically so the account timeline shows the meeting happened.

items.cadence: Near real time by push notification; a 15-minute poll reconciles anything missed

screenshots.caption: The scheduling panel on a customer record showing available slots after free-busy checking, with travel buffers indicated for an on-site visit.
screenshots.note: Capture with a genuinely busy calendar so the blocked slots are visible. Date stamp required.

screenshots.caption: The resulting Google Calendar event with the RFQ number in the description, the plant address as the location and buffer events either side.
screenshots.note: Capture in Google Calendar itself. Date stamp required; blur other calendar entries.

screenshots.caption: The activity record showing attendee responses, including one declined customer invitation.
screenshots.note: Capture a genuine decline rather than staging one. Date stamp required.

setup: In KanchanFlow, open Settings, Integrations, Google Calendar and click Connect. Each user connects their own calendar.
Authorise on Google's consent screen. We request calendar read and write on the connected account, and free-busy for scheduling.
Choose which of your Google calendars is the working calendar. People with several calendars must pick one; we do not write to all of them.
Set which CRM activity types create calendar events. Site visits and customer meetings usually should; internal task reminders usually should not.
Configure travel buffers by activity type. A site visit buffer of sixty minutes each way is a reasonable default that you can override per customer.
Set reminder defaults per activity type.
Decide whether customer contacts are invited as attendees. Some shops prefer to invite only internal staff and send the customer a separate confirmation.
Turn on automatic linking of calendar events that include known customer contacts, if you want unscheduled meetings to appear on the account timeline.
Set working hours in the connector so the slot picker does not offer a customer a seven in the morning site visit.
Book one test site visit from a customer record and confirm the buffers and the address are correct in Google Calendar.
limitations: Each user connects their own calendar. There is no domain-wide connection, so a scheduling change made for the whole team means everyone reconnects.
We write to one selected calendar per user. Events on other calendars are read for free-busy only, and secondary calendars cannot be written to.
Travel buffers use a fixed drive-time value you configure per customer. We do not call a maps service and we do not adjust for traffic, so a buffer is an estimate, not a routing calculation.
Recurring events sync as a series. Editing a single occurrence in Google Calendar can desynchronise that occurrence from the CRM activity, and we do not attempt to reconcile individual exceptions.
We do not manage room or resource bookings, and we do not book equipment or machine time. This is a customer-facing calendar integration, not a shop scheduling system.
Free-busy accuracy depends on people actually keeping their calendar current. The connector cannot know about a visit that was agreed on the phone and never booked.

troubleshooting.error: Events appear on the wrong calendar
troubleshooting.cause: The user has several calendars and the working calendar selection points at the wrong one.
troubleshooting.fix: Change the selection in the connector. Existing events do not move; they must be moved in Google Calendar by hand.

troubleshooting.error: Customer says they never received an invitation
troubleshooting.cause: Attendee invitations are disabled in the connector, or the customer's mail server rejected the invite.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the attendee setting, then check the activity for a delivery failure. Some corporate mail systems strip calendar invitations from external senders entirely.

troubleshooting.error: Slot picker offers times the user is busy
troubleshooting.cause: The conflicting event lives on a calendar not included in free-busy, or is marked as free rather than busy.
troubleshooting.fix: Add the calendar to the free-busy set in connector settings and ask the user to mark blocking events as busy.

troubleshooting.error: A rescheduled meeting shows two different times
troubleshooting.cause: It was rescheduled in Google Calendar and then again in the CRM before the sync cycle completed.
troubleshooting.fix: Open the activity and use Resync from calendar, which treats Google as authoritative for time. Agree with your team to reschedule in one place.

troubleshooting.error: Travel buffers are wrong for a distant customer
troubleshooting.cause: The drive time is set at the global default rather than per customer.
troubleshooting.fix: Set the drive-time value on the customer record. There is no automatic distance calculation and we would rather say so than have you rely on a number we did not compute.

faqs.q: Does it schedule machine or production time?
faqs.a: No. This is a customer-facing calendar for visits, reviews and calls. Production scheduling belongs in your ERP or MES, and we are not one.

faqs.q: Which tiers include calendar sync?
faqs.a: All tiers. Meeting summarisation, which is a separate AI feature, consumes credits at three per meeting under thirty minutes.

faqs.q: Can I invite customers directly?
faqs.a: Yes, if you enable attendee invitations. Some shops prefer not to, because a customer declining an invitation is more visible than a customer not replying to an email.

faqs.q: Does it handle travel time?
faqs.a: It adds buffer events using a drive time you configure per customer. It does not calculate routes or check traffic, and the buffer is only as good as the number you set.

faqs.q: What if someone reschedules in Google Calendar?
faqs.a: The change flows back to the CRM activity within a cycle. Google is treated as authoritative for the time of an event, because that is where people actually reschedule.

faqs.q: Does it work with Google Workspace calendars shared across a team?
faqs.a: It reads shared calendars for free-busy. It writes only to the connected user's selected working calendar.

items.tiers: All tiers — meeting summarisation is a separate AI feature that consumes credits

items.name: Zoom
items.tagline: Create a Zoom link from the record for a drawing walkthrough, and get the recording and an AI summary back on the account timeline.
items.metaDescription: Zoom integration for manufacturing CRM: create meetings from customer records, attach recordings and transcripts, summarise drawing reviews.
items.answer: KanchanFlow, the RFQ-to-Order CRM, creates Zoom meetings from a customer or RFQ record and brings the recording, transcript and participation details back onto the timeline. Where you enable it, meeting summarisation turns a drawing review into written follow-up actions at three to six AI credits per meeting.
intro: The drawing review call is where a quote is really settled. Tolerances get relaxed, a finish gets changed, a delivery date gets agreed, and thirty minutes later nobody has written any of it down. The quote goes out reflecting what the estimator remembers, which is not always what was said.

This connector attaches that call to the record. The meeting is created from the RFQ, the recording and transcript come back to it, and the summarisation agent extracts the decisions and follow-ups as text you can check against the quote before you send it. The point is not the recording; it is the written record of what changed.

syncTo.detail: Created with the topic carrying the customer and RFQ number, the agenda carrying the record link, and the correct host from the CRM activity owner.
Internal attendees and customer contacts from the activity, so the join link reaches everyone without a separate email.
Waiting room, recording policy and passcode applied from the template you configure, so a customer call is not accidentally set to record when your policy says it should not be.
Changing the activity updates the Zoom meeting rather than leaving a stale link circulating.

syncFrom.detail: Cloud recordings and their transcripts attach to the activity, subject to your Zoom plan including cloud recording.
Who joined, when and for how long, which is a blunt but useful signal of whether the customer's technical people actually attended.
Whether the meeting occurred, was cancelled or nobody joined, written to the activity so no-shows are visible in the pipeline.
Where enabled, a structured summary with decisions and follow-up actions, generated from the transcript at three credits for meetings up to thirty minutes and six credits for thirty to sixty.

items.cadence: Real time by webhook for meeting events and recordings; summaries generate within minutes of the recording being available

screenshots.caption: The activity panel on an RFQ showing the Create Zoom meeting control with the meeting template and recording policy selected.
screenshots.note: Capture from a live workspace. Date stamp required.

screenshots.caption: A completed activity showing the recording attached, participation times, and the AI summary with extracted follow-up actions.
screenshots.note: Capture from a genuine recorded internal test call, never a customer call. Date stamp required.

screenshots.caption: The connector's recording policy settings showing retention and which meeting types may be recorded.
screenshots.note: Capture the genuine settings page. Date stamp required.

setup: Confirm your Zoom plan. Cloud recording and transcripts require a paid Zoom plan; a free account can create meetings but nothing comes back afterwards.

Decide your recording policy before connecting. Recording a customer without clear consent is a legal problem in several US states and in most of Europe, and this is a decision for your business, not a default we should set.
In KanchanFlow, open Settings, Integrations, Zoom and click Connect. Each meeting host connects their own Zoom account.
Authorise on Zoom's consent screen. On some Zoom accounts the marketplace app must be pre-approved by a Zoom administrator first.
Configure meeting templates: waiting room, passcode, and whether recording starts automatically. Create separate templates for internal and customer meetings.
Set which CRM activity types can create Zoom meetings.
Set the recording retention period in the connector, and make sure it is no longer than your own data retention policy allows.
Enable meeting summarisation only where you want it, and be aware it consumes AI credits per meeting.
Configure who can read recordings. By default only the activity owner and their manager can, which is usually correct.
Run a test meeting with a colleague, record it, and confirm the recording, transcript and summary all arrive on the activity.
Tell your customers you record, if you record. Doing so is both the legal position in many places and the decent one.
limitations: Cloud recording, transcripts and therefore summaries require a paid Zoom plan. On a free plan this connector schedules meetings and nothing else.

Transcript accuracy on a shop-floor call with background machine noise is poor, and a summary built on a poor transcript is worse than no summary. Do not rely on it for anything you would not re-read.
Recording consent is your responsibility. We provide the policy controls; we do not and cannot enforce the law of the jurisdiction your customer is in.
Recordings consume workspace storage against your tier's allowance. A shop recording every call will fill a Starter tier's 10 GB quickly.
We do not support Zoom Phone, Zoom Contact Center, or webinars. Meetings only.
Summarisation is an AI feature and will occasionally attribute a decision to the wrong participant or miss a caveat. It is a starting point for a human to correct, not a record of what was agreed.

troubleshooting.error: Connect fails with App not pre-approved
troubleshooting.cause: The Zoom account restricts marketplace apps and an administrator has not approved ours.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask your Zoom administrator to pre-approve the app in the Zoom marketplace admin settings, then reconnect.

troubleshooting.error: Meeting created but no recording appears
troubleshooting.cause: The Zoom plan does not include cloud recording, or the meeting was recorded locally to the host's machine.
troubleshooting.fix: Local recordings never leave the host's computer and cannot be fetched. Set cloud recording in the meeting template if you want recordings on the record.

troubleshooting.error: Summary is inaccurate or misses a key decision
troubleshooting.cause: The transcript quality was poor, usually from background noise or several people speaking at once.
troubleshooting.fix: Read the transcript, correct the summary on the activity, and treat the summary as a draft. Recording from a quiet room materially improves both.

troubleshooting.error: Storage warnings after enabling recording sync
troubleshooting.cause: Recordings are counted against your tier's storage allowance.
troubleshooting.fix: Shorten the retention period, restrict which activity types sync recordings, or add storage. On Starter, extra 10 GB is $10 per month.

troubleshooting.error: Customer joined but participation shows nobody attended
troubleshooting.cause: The customer joined a different meeting, usually an old link from a rescheduled activity.
troubleshooting.fix: Reschedule from the CRM rather than creating a new meeting manually, so the link circulating is always the current one.

faqs.q: Do I need a paid Zoom plan?
faqs.a: To schedule, no. For recordings, transcripts and summaries, yes. We will not pretend a free plan gives you the part that matters.

faqs.q: Which tiers include Zoom?
faqs.a: All tiers for meeting creation. Meeting summarisation consumes AI credits: three for a meeting up to thirty minutes, six for thirty to sixty.

faqs.q: Is recording on by default?
faqs.a: No. Recording is off until you configure a meeting template that enables it, and we deliberately make you make that decision.

faqs.q: How good are the summaries?
faqs.a: Good on a quiet call with clear speakers, poor on a noisy shop-floor call. Treat every summary as a draft a human should check before it informs a quote.

faqs.q: Where are recordings stored?
faqs.a: In your workspace, against your storage allowance, with the retention period you set. They are visible to the activity owner and their manager unless you widen that.

faqs.q: Does it work with Microsoft Teams meetings?
faqs.a: Teams meeting links are created through the Outlook connector's calendar sync. This connector is Zoom-specific, and recording capture is Zoom-only today.

items.tiers: All tiers — meeting summarisation consumes AI credits (3 credits ≤30 min, 6 credits 30–60 min)

items.name: Cloudbeds
items.tagline: For manufacturers who supply the hospitality trade: pull property and room-count data from a customer's Cloudbeds account into the CRM.
items.metaDescription: Cloudbeds integration for manufacturing CRM: pull property and room-count data for manufacturers supplying contract furniture, FF&E and equipment.
items.answer: KanchanFlow, the RFQ-to-Order CRM, reads property records, room counts and property groupings from a customer's Cloudbeds account so a manufacturer supplying contract furniture, FF&E or commercial kitchen equipment can size a fit-out from real data. It is the narrowest connector we ship and it suits one specific kind of shop.
intro: This connector exists for a specific customer type: manufacturers whose buyers are hotels and hospitality groups. If you make contract furniture, casegoods, commercial laundry equipment or kitchen fit-outs, the size of the opportunity is a function of properties and room counts, and those numbers live in the customer's property management system.

Where a hospitality customer is willing to grant read access, we pull their property list, room counts and property groupings onto the account. An estimator sizing a refurbishment then quotes against a real room count rather than a number somebody remembered from a site visit two years ago.

syncTo.detail: The only outbound call is an authenticated read of the property list on the customer's account, scoped to the properties you selected during setup.
We never create, modify or cancel a reservation. The scope is not requested, so the capability does not exist even if someone asked for it.
We never write rates, restrictions or availability. A manufacturer has no business changing a hotel's pricing and we did not build the path.
We never read or write guest records. Guest scopes are not requested, which is the point of the second screenshot on this page.

syncFrom.detail: Each property on the connected Cloudbeds account, with name, address and city, mapped to plants or sites on the CRM customer record.
Total rooms and room types per property, which is the figure that sizes a furniture or equipment fit-out quote.
How properties are grouped in the customer's account, which usually reveals the real purchasing structure of a hospitality group.
Active or inactive, so a closed property is not quoted for a refurbishment.

items.cadence: Once daily; property data does not change often enough to justify anything faster

screenshots.caption: A hospitality customer record showing the property list pulled from Cloudbeds, with room counts per property and the group structure.
screenshots.note: Capture from a sandbox or a customer who has explicitly consented to being shown. Date stamp required; property names must be masked.

screenshots.caption: The connector's scope screen showing that only property and room data is requested, with reservation and guest scopes visibly absent.
screenshots.note: Capture the genuine scope list, because the absence of guest scopes is the point of the screenshot. Date stamp required.

screenshots.caption: A fit-out quote sized from the synced room count, showing the room count field bound to the property record.
screenshots.note: Capture a real quote in a sandbox workspace. Date stamp required.

setup: Confirm this connector applies to you. If your customers are not hospitality properties, it has no function and you should skip it.
Ask your customer whether they will grant read access to their Cloudbeds account. This is their data and their decision, and most conversations end here.
Have the customer create a read-only API user in Cloudbeds scoped to property data only.
In KanchanFlow, open Settings, Integrations, Cloudbeds and add a connection for that customer, entering the credentials they provided.
Select which properties to sync. A large group may have properties that are not yours to quote.
Map properties to the plant or site records on the CRM customer so quotes reference the right property.
Map room types to your product lines if you quote different products by room type.
Run the first sync and check the room counts against whatever you believed them to be. Expect discrepancies; that is the reason for doing this.
Set the refresh to daily and leave it there.
Document with the customer what you are reading and why, in writing. Access to a customer's operational system should never be an informal arrangement.
limitations: This connector requires your customer to grant you access to their system, which most will not. Realistically it applies to a small number of long-standing accounts, and we would rather say that plainly than imply it is widely usable.
Read-only, permanently. There is no write path and we will not build one.

We never read reservations, rates, occupancy or any guest data, and we do not request those scopes. If you were hoping to see occupancy to time a refurbishment pitch, this connector will not give you that.
One Cloudbeds connection per CRM customer. A group with several separate Cloudbeds accounts needs one connection each.
Room counts reflect what the customer maintains in Cloudbeds, which is often out of date after a renovation. It is better data than a memory, not authoritative data.

This is our lowest-usage connector by a wide margin. It receives the same quarterly regression as everything else, but it gets far less real-world exercise, so unusual configurations are more likely to surface problems here.

troubleshooting.error: Authentication fails with insufficient scope
troubleshooting.cause: The API user the customer created has fewer permissions than property read.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask the customer to grant property read on the API user. Do not ask them to widen scopes beyond that; we do not use anything else.

troubleshooting.error: Room counts differ from what the customer told you
troubleshooting.cause: The Cloudbeds configuration was not updated after a renovation or a room-type change.
troubleshooting.fix: Treat the sync as a prompt for a conversation, not as a correction. Confirm the count with the customer and record the agreed figure on the property.

troubleshooting.error: Properties appear that are not yours to quote
troubleshooting.cause: The credentials cover the customer's whole group.
troubleshooting.fix: Deselect them in the property selection screen. Only selected properties are stored.

troubleshooting.error: Sync stopped after the customer rotated credentials
troubleshooting.cause: The customer's IT changed the API user password.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask for the new credentials. This connector breaks whenever the customer's own housekeeping changes, which is a reason to check it quarterly.

troubleshooting.error: Duplicate plant records on the customer
troubleshooting.cause: Properties were synced before existing plant records were mapped.
troubleshooting.fix: Merge the plants and set the mapping in the connector so future syncs bind to the surviving record.

faqs.q: Why does a manufacturing CRM integrate with a hotel system?
faqs.a: Because manufacturers who supply hospitality need room counts and property lists to size a quote. If you do not supply that trade, this connector is not for you and switching it off costs you nothing.

faqs.q: Do you read guest or reservation data?
faqs.a: No, and we do not request those scopes. Property, room count, grouping and status only.

faqs.q: Which tiers include it?
faqs.a: Professional and Enterprise. It depends on the multi-plant customer structure that Starter does not have.

faqs.q: Will my customer agree to this?
faqs.a: Most will not, and that is a reasonable position for them to take. It tends to work only with long-standing accounts where you already do renovation planning together.

faqs.q: Can it write a reservation or block rooms?
faqs.a: No. Read-only, permanently, by design.

faqs.q: Is it worth setting up?
faqs.a: Only for a shop whose quotes are sized by room count. For everyone else it is the least useful of our twenty-six connectors and we will tell you so.

items.tiers: Professional and Enterprise

items.name: Shopify
items.tagline: Pull direct and B2B Shopify orders into the same pipeline as your RFQs, so catalogue sales and custom work share one customer record.
items.metaDescription: Shopify integration for manufacturing CRM: sync orders, customers and B2B company accounts so catalogue and custom quote work share one record.
items.answer: KanchanFlow, the RFQ-to-Order CRM, syncs Shopify orders, customers and B2B company accounts so a manufacturer selling both a standard catalogue and custom work sees them on one customer record. A repeat catalogue buyer who then requests a custom part is recognised as the same account rather than as a new lead.
intro: A growing number of job shops now run a Shopify store alongside the quoting business: standard parts, replacement components, tooling, or a small product line built from the same capability. The two channels usually live entirely apart, and the customer who buys standard parts online is invisible when they email asking for something custom.

This connector joins them. Shopify orders and customers sync into the CRM against the same accounts your RFQs use, including B2B company accounts and their price lists where you use Shopify's B2B features. The result is one view of the account, which is also what makes a cross-sell conversation possible.

syncTo.detail: Where you enable it, we write a tag to the Shopify customer reflecting their CRM segment, so your storefront can offer the right price list or content.
Where a Shopify order originated from a CRM quote, the quote number is written to the order note for reconciliation.
We do not manage products, inventory, pricing or fulfilment in Shopify. Your store is run from Shopify by whoever runs it today.

syncFrom.detail: Order number, date, line items with SKU and quantity, discounts, shipping and total, posted to the customer's timeline.
Name, email, phone and default address, matched to existing CRM accounts on email first and company name second.
Where you use Shopify B2B, the company, its locations and its assigned price list, mapped to CRM accounts and plants.
Fulfilment status and tracking numbers so a salesperson answering a where-is-my-order call does not have to open Shopify.
Refunded and cancelled orders, so account value figures in the CRM are net rather than gross.

items.cadence: Real time by webhook for orders and fulfilments; a 15-minute reconciliation sweep backfills anything missed

setup: Confirm who administers your Shopify store. You need a staff account with permission to install apps and read orders and customers.
In KanchanFlow, open Settings, Integrations, Shopify and enter your store's myshopify domain.
Complete the install on Shopify's own permission screen. We request read access to orders, customers, fulfilments and, where you use it, B2B companies.
Choose the historical import window. Ninety days is the default and is usually enough to establish which customers are repeat buyers.
Set the customer matching rule. Email primary and company name secondary works for most stores.
Decide whether Shopify orders create CRM orders or only timeline entries. Timeline entries are the safer starting point unless you intend to manage fulfilment commitments from the CRM.
If you use Shopify B2B, map company locations to CRM plants so quotes and orders reference the same sites.
Enable customer tag write-back only if your storefront actually uses tags for segmentation. Otherwise leave it off.
Set which order statuses matter. Most shops ignore draft and abandoned orders in the CRM.
Run the historical import outside business hours; a large store's ninety-day import takes time.
Place one test order and confirm it appears on the right customer record within a minute.
limitations: One Shopify store per workspace. Manufacturers running separate stores per brand need a workspace per store or must choose which store syncs.
We do not sync products or inventory. Stock levels are Shopify's business and a CRM should not be a second source of truth for them.
We do not write orders into Shopify. A custom quote accepted in the CRM does not create a Shopify order, because custom work does not belong in a catalogue checkout.
Shopify's API rate limits apply. A very large historical import is throttled and can take hours to complete.

Customer matching across channels is imperfect. A buyer who uses a personal email at checkout and a work email for RFQs will create two records until someone merges them, and no matching rule solves that reliably.
Shopify B2B features are only available on Shopify Plus. On other plans the company account fields simply do not exist and that part of the connector is inert.

troubleshooting.error: Orders sync but do not attach to the right account
troubleshooting.cause: The checkout email differs from the email on the CRM account.
troubleshooting.fix: Add the checkout email as a secondary address on the contact, or merge the accounts. Enabling company-name matching as a secondary rule reduces but does not eliminate this.

troubleshooting.error: Historical import appears stuck
troubleshooting.cause: Shopify is throttling the request rate on a large store.
troubleshooting.fix: Leave it. The import resumes automatically and reports progress on the connector page. Do not restart it; restarting begins the throttled work again.

troubleshooting.error: B2B company accounts are missing
troubleshooting.cause: The store is not on Shopify Plus, so the B2B objects do not exist.
troubleshooting.fix: Nothing to fix on our side. Company accounts require Shopify Plus and the connector hides those fields when they are unavailable.

troubleshooting.error: Refunded orders still counted in account value
troubleshooting.cause: The refund webhook was missed and the reconciliation sweep has not yet run.
troubleshooting.fix: Wait one cycle or press Sync now on the customer. If refunds are persistently missed, check the webhook subscriptions on the Shopify app page.

troubleshooting.error: Customer tags are not appearing in Shopify
troubleshooting.cause: Tag write-back is disabled, which is the default.
troubleshooting.fix: Enable it in connector settings. Only enable it if your storefront actually uses tags; writing tags nobody reads just adds noise to your customer records.

faqs.q: Why would a job shop use Shopify?
faqs.a: For standard parts, replacement components and tooling that do not need a quote. Plenty of shops run a small catalogue alongside custom work, and this connector stops those two views of a customer being separate.

faqs.q: Which tiers include Shopify?
faqs.a: Professional and Enterprise. It relies on the unlimited contacts and multi-plant customer structure that Starter does not have.

faqs.q: Does it manage inventory?
faqs.a: No. Inventory belongs in Shopify or your ERP. We are the customer record, not a stock system.

faqs.q: Can a CRM quote become a Shopify order?
faqs.a: No. Custom quoted work does not belong in a catalogue checkout, and we did not build that path.

faqs.q: Do B2B company accounts sync?
faqs.a: Yes, on Shopify Plus. On other plans those objects do not exist in Shopify at all.

faqs.q: What about abandoned checkouts?
faqs.a: Not synced. They generate more noise than signal for a manufacturer, and we would rather leave them out than fill your pipeline with them.

items.tiers: Professional and Enterprise

items.name: Shiprocket
items.tagline: Create a Shiprocket shipment from a dispatched order and push tracking onto the customer record. In development, target Wave 1 Month 4.
items.metaDescription: Shiprocket integration for manufacturing CRM: create shipments from dispatched orders and sync AWB tracking. In development, target Wave 1 Month 4.
items.answer: KanchanFlow, the RFQ-to-Order CRM, is building a Shiprocket connector that creates a shipment from a dispatched order, returns the AWB number and pushes tracking milestones onto the customer timeline. It is in development with a Wave 1 Month 4 target and is not usable in production today.
intro: Where is my order is the question that consumes the most sales time after a job ships, and answering it usually means opening a courier portal, finding a docket number in an email, and reading a status back over the phone. None of that requires a salesperson, but all of it takes one.

The Shiprocket connector will create the shipment from the dispatched order, so the AWB is generated against the order rather than typed into a portal, and the tracking milestones land on the customer timeline as they happen. This is in development. Everything on this page describes what is being built, and the status badge will change to Live when it is genuinely in production.
items.frame: This connector is for USA manufacturers with India operations, India-based contract customers, or manufacturers exporting to India. Shiprocket is an Indian aggregator and serves shipments originating in India.

syncTo.detail: Planned: consignee name, address, phone and pin code from the order's ship-to, together with package count, dimensions and declared value, submitted to create a shipment.
Planned: box dimensions and weight per package from the packing list, which is what drives courier selection and rate.
Planned: your preferred courier or Shiprocket's recommendation, selectable per shipment and defaultable per customer.
Planned: invoice number and e-way bill number where one exists, so the paperwork travelling with the consignment matches the order.
Planned: pickup scheduling against your registered pickup location, so a dispatch does not need a separate portal visit.

syncFrom.detail: Planned: the assigned AWB and the courier that took the consignment, written to the order.
Planned: picked up, in transit, out for delivery, delivered, with timestamps on the customer timeline.
Planned: undelivered attempts, address issues and RTO initiation, which are the events that actually need a salesperson to act.
Planned: the delivery confirmation and, where the courier supplies it, the proof of delivery document attached to the order.
Planned: the freight cost charged, so landed cost against an order can be compared to what was quoted.

items.cadence: Planned: real time by webhook for tracking events, with a 30-minute reconciliation poll

setup: Planned: create or identify your Shiprocket account and complete KYC and pickup location registration.
Planned: generate API credentials in the Shiprocket dashboard under API settings.
Planned: in KanchanFlow, open Settings, Integrations, Shiprocket and enter the credentials.
Planned: map your pickup locations to the CRM plants that dispatch from them.
Planned: set default package dimensions per product line so a dispatcher is not measuring every box.
Planned: configure courier preference rules by destination pin code and weight band.
Planned: map order statuses so that only genuinely dispatched orders create shipments.
Planned: set up the webhook endpoint for tracking events from the connector page.
Planned: define who may create and cancel shipments; this spends money and should not be open to everyone.
Planned: run a test shipment to a colleague's address and follow it through to delivery before using it for a customer order.
limitations: This connector is not available yet. The target is Wave 1 Month 4, and until it ships nothing on this page can be used. We publish it now so you can plan, not so you can buy something that does not exist.
Planned: Shiprocket serves shipments originating in India. It will not handle a USA-origin dispatch, and we will not imply otherwise.
Planned: courier serviceability, rates and delivery estimates all come from Shiprocket. When a pin code is not serviceable, we will report that rather than suggest an alternative we cannot guarantee.
Planned: freight cost reconciliation will be at shipment level only. We will not reconcile Shiprocket's weight discrepancy charges, which are a common and unwelcome surprise on this platform.
Planned: no international shipping support in the first release, even where Shiprocket offers it.
Planned: shipment cancellation after pickup will not be possible from the CRM, because it is not reliably possible in the underlying platform either.

troubleshooting.error: Planned: Shipment creation fails with pickup location not registered
troubleshooting.cause: The pickup location referenced on the plant is not registered and verified in Shiprocket.
troubleshooting.fix: Register and verify the pickup location in the Shiprocket dashboard, then re-map it to the plant in connector settings.

troubleshooting.error: Planned: Pin code not serviceable
troubleshooting.cause: No courier on your Shiprocket account serves that destination for the selected weight band.
troubleshooting.fix: Check serviceability in Shiprocket, and consider a different courier partner. We report the platform's answer; we cannot create serviceability that does not exist.

troubleshooting.error: Planned: AWB assigned but no tracking events arrive
troubleshooting.cause: The webhook endpoint is not configured, or the courier is slow to scan the first event.
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm the webhook in the Shiprocket dashboard. The reconciliation poll will pick up events within thirty minutes regardless.

troubleshooting.error: Planned: Weight discrepancy charge appears after delivery
troubleshooting.cause: The courier's measured weight exceeded the declared weight.
troubleshooting.fix: This is settled between you and Shiprocket. We show the shipping charge we were told at creation and flag when a later charge differs, but we do not dispute it for you.

troubleshooting.error: Planned: Shipment created against the wrong address
troubleshooting.cause: The order's ship-to was edited after dispatch was raised.
troubleshooting.fix: Cancel before pickup if you still can, and re-create. After pickup, the courier's redirection process is the only route.

faqs.q: When will this be available?
faqs.a: The target is Wave 1 Month 4. The status badge on this page says Building and will change to Live only when it is in production. We do not move badges early.

faqs.q: Can I use it today?
faqs.a: No. Everything described here is in development. If you need Indian dispatch tracking now, keep using the Shiprocket dashboard.

faqs.q: Which tiers will include it?
faqs.a: Professional and Enterprise, because it depends on webhook capacity that Starter does not include.

faqs.q: Will it handle international shipments?
faqs.a: Not in the first release, even though Shiprocket offers international services. We would rather ship domestic Indian dispatch properly than ship both badly.

faqs.q: Will freight cost feed into landed cost analysis?
faqs.a: At shipment level, yes. Weight discrepancy charges raised after delivery will be flagged but not reconciled automatically.

faqs.q: What happens if the target date slips?
faqs.a: The target on this page changes and the changelog records why. We do not quietly leave a stale date on a page.

items.name: Delhivery
items.tagline: Direct Delhivery waybills and tracking for shops shipping heavy or palletised freight in India. In development, target Wave 1 Month 4.
items.metaDescription: Delhivery integration for manufacturing CRM: create waybills and track heavy or palletised freight. In development, target Wave 1 Month 4.
items.answer: KanchanFlow, the RFQ-to-Order CRM, is building a direct Delhivery connector for waybill creation and freight tracking, aimed at shops moving heavy or palletised consignments rather than parcels. It is in development with a Wave 1 Month 4 target and cannot be used in production today.
intro: Manufacturing freight is not e-commerce parcels. A consignment is heavy, sometimes palletised, occasionally on a dedicated vehicle, and the questions that matter are whether it was picked up, where it is now, and whether the delivery paperwork came back signed. Aggregator tooling built for parcels handles that badly.

The Delhivery connector goes direct rather than through an aggregator, which gives better handling of B2B and heavy consignments. Waybills are created from the dispatched order, tracking scans land on the customer timeline, and the proof of delivery attaches to the order. This is in development and the page will keep saying so until it ships.
items.frame: This connector is for USA manufacturers with India operations, India-based contract customers, or manufacturers exporting to India. Delhivery carries shipments originating in India.

syncTo.detail: Planned: consignee details, pickup location, package count, actual and volumetric weight, declared value and payment mode, submitted to generate a waybill.
Planned: parcel, heavy or part-truckload selection, which is the distinction that makes a direct integration worth having over an aggregator.
Planned: the e-way bill number generated through the ClearTax connector, attached to the consignment so documentation travels together.
Planned: pickup scheduling against a registered warehouse location with a requested time window.
Planned: waybill cancellation before manifest, from the order record, restricted to users holding the dispatch role.

syncFrom.detail: Planned: the assigned waybill and whether it has been manifested, on the order record.
Planned: every scan from pickup through to delivery, with location and timestamp, on the customer timeline.
Planned: the signed proof of delivery document attached to the order, which for B2B freight is often what a customer's accounts department wants before paying.
Planned: failed delivery attempts, address exceptions and return-to-origin events surfaced as tasks rather than buried in a portal.
Planned: the charged freight amount, for landed cost comparison against what was quoted.

items.cadence: Planned: real time by webhook for scan events, with a 30-minute reconciliation poll

screenshots.caption: The dispatch panel showing consignment type selection for a palletised shipment with actual and volumetric weight entered.
screenshots.note: Cannot be captured until release. Do not publish a mockup; capture at release with a date stamp.

screenshots.caption: An order timeline showing Delhivery scan events with locations from pickup through to delivery.

screenshots.note: Capture at release with the signature and consignee name masked in the product. Date stamp required.

setup: Planned: obtain a Delhivery B2B or express account and complete onboarding, including registered warehouse locations.
Planned: request API credentials from your Delhivery account manager. Direct API access is not self-service.
Planned: in KanchanFlow, open Settings, Integrations, Delhivery and enter the credentials and client warehouse names exactly as registered.
Planned: map warehouses to the CRM plants that dispatch from them. Warehouse names must match Delhivery's records character for character.
Planned: configure consignment type defaults per product line, so heavy fabrications do not default to parcel handling.
Planned: set volumetric weight rules matching your Delhivery contract, because the divisor differs by agreement.
Planned: connect the ClearTax e-way bill reference if you generate e-way bills, so documentation is attached at creation.
Planned: configure the webhook for scan events from the connector page.
Planned: restrict waybill creation and cancellation to the dispatch role.
Planned: run one test consignment to a known address and follow it to delivery, including retrieving the proof of delivery, before live use.
limitations: This connector is not available yet. Target is Wave 1 Month 4. Nothing here can be used today and we publish it so you can plan rather than so you can buy.
Planned: Delhivery direct API access is granted by Delhivery, not by us. If your account does not have it, the connector cannot work and that is a commercial conversation with them.
Planned: warehouse names must match Delhivery's registration exactly. This is the single most common cause of failed waybill creation on this platform and no amount of connector logic removes it.
Planned: rate calculation will not be included in the first release. We create waybills and track; we do not quote freight.
Planned: part-truckload and full-truckload consignments will be supported for tracking, but pickup scheduling for dedicated vehicles will still be arranged with Delhivery directly.
Planned: no international shipping in the first release.

troubleshooting.error: Planned: Waybill creation fails with client warehouse not found
troubleshooting.cause: The warehouse name does not match Delhivery's registered name exactly, including case and spacing.
troubleshooting.fix: Copy the warehouse name verbatim from the Delhivery panel into the connector mapping. Do not retype it.

troubleshooting.error: Planned: Volumetric weight rejected
troubleshooting.cause: The volumetric divisor configured does not match your Delhivery contract.
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm the divisor with your account manager and set it in connector settings. It differs between express and B2B agreements.

troubleshooting.error: Planned: No scan events after pickup
troubleshooting.cause: The consignment was manifested but not yet scanned at a hub, or the webhook is unconfigured.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the webhook first. Genuine first-scan delays of several hours are normal for B2B freight and are not a fault.

troubleshooting.error: Planned: Proof of delivery missing after delivery
troubleshooting.cause: Delhivery uploads proof of delivery on its own schedule, sometimes a day after the delivery scan.
troubleshooting.fix: The connector retries for seventy-two hours. After that, request it from Delhivery directly.

troubleshooting.error: Planned: Consignment defaulted to parcel handling
troubleshooting.cause: No consignment type rule matched the product line on the order.
troubleshooting.fix: Set the consignment type default for that product line. Heavy fabrication moving as a parcel is expensive and slow.

faqs.q: Why Delhivery as well as Shiprocket?
faqs.a: Shiprocket aggregates couriers and suits parcels. Delhivery direct handles heavy and palletised B2B freight far better, which is what most manufacturers actually ship.

faqs.q: When will it be available?
faqs.a: Wave 1 Month 4 is the target. The badge stays on Building until it is genuinely in production.

faqs.q: Which tiers will include it?
faqs.a: Professional and Enterprise, because it depends on webhook capacity Starter does not include.

faqs.q: Will it quote freight rates?
faqs.a: Not in the first release. It creates waybills and tracks consignments. Rate quoting is a separate problem and we would rather do this part properly first.

faqs.q: Do I need a special Delhivery account?
faqs.a: You need direct API access, which Delhivery grants case by case. A standard e-commerce seller account may not have it.

faqs.q: Will proof of delivery be attached automatically?
faqs.a: That is the plan, with a seventy-two hour retry window, because Delhivery uploads it on its own schedule rather than at the moment of delivery.

items.name: FedEx
items.tagline: Label creation, rating and tracking for USA domestic and export shipments. In development, targeted at Wave 2 Q2 2027.
items.metaDescription: FedEx integration for manufacturing CRM: create labels, rate and track USA domestic and export freight from the order. Target Wave 2 Q2 2027.
items.answer: KanchanFlow, the RFQ-to-Order CRM, is building a FedEx connector for label creation, rating and tracking on USA domestic and export shipments, including the commercial invoice data an international consignment needs. It is a Wave 2 item with a Q2 2027 target and is the furthest out of anything in our catalogue.
intro: FedEx is the connector USA manufacturers ask for most often and it is the one furthest from shipping, which is an uncomfortable thing to write on a page whose purpose is to sell software. We are writing it anyway, because a roadmap that hides its own gaps is worthless.

When it ships, it will create labels from the dispatched order, rate a shipment before it is quoted, track it to delivery and carry the commercial invoice data an export consignment needs. Until then, the honest answer is that you will keep using FedEx Ship Manager, and this page will say so.

syncTo.detail: Planned: recipient details, package dimensions and weight, service level and payment terms, submitted to generate a shipping label for the dispatched order.
Planned: a rating call before dispatch, and optionally at quoting time, so freight on a quote reflects a real rate rather than an estimate somebody remembered.
Planned: harmonised codes, country of origin, declared value and incoterms for international consignments, which is where most export shipping errors actually originate.
Planned: pickup scheduling against your registered account and location.
Planned: shipping billed to the customer's own FedEx account, which is how a large share of manufacturing freight is actually paid for.

syncFrom.detail: Planned: the tracking number and the printable label attached to the order.
Planned: service options with cost and transit time, so a dispatcher can choose knowingly rather than defaulting to overnight.
Planned: every scan through to delivery, on the customer timeline.
Planned: delivery confirmation and, where the service includes it, the signature image.
Planned: delivery exceptions, customs holds and address corrections, raised as tasks.

items.cadence: Planned: real time tracking updates by subscription, with a 30-minute reconciliation poll

screenshots.caption: The dispatch panel with FedEx service options, rates and transit times returned for a real shipment.
screenshots.note: Cannot be captured until release; this connector is targeted at Wave 2 Q2 2027. Do not publish a mockup.

screenshots.caption: A generated FedEx label attached to the order record with the tracking number visible.
screenshots.note: Capture at release with recipient details masked. Date stamp required.

setup: Planned: obtain a FedEx developer account and register an application for production API access.
Planned: link your FedEx shipping account number and complete FedEx's production certification, which is a review process rather than an instant approval.
Planned: in KanchanFlow, open Settings, Integrations, FedEx and enter the API credentials and account number.
Planned: map ship-from locations to the CRM plants that dispatch from them.
Planned: configure default service levels and package types per product line.
Planned: set up billing rules, including third-party and recipient billing for customers who ship on their own account.
Planned: configure the commercial invoice defaults for exports, including your default incoterms and country of origin.
Planned: set harmonised codes on your item master, because an export label without them will fail at customs, not at the connector.
Planned: restrict label creation to the dispatch role.
Planned: run test labels in the FedEx sandbox, then one live low-value domestic shipment before using it on an export consignment.
limitations: This is a Wave 2 connector targeted at Q2 2027, which is the furthest-out item in our catalogue. If FedEx integration is a purchase requirement for you today, we are not the right choice and you should know that before you trial us.
Planned: FedEx requires production certification of the application before live label creation is enabled, and that timeline is theirs, not ours.
Planned: rating accuracy depends on your negotiated FedEx rates being correctly associated with the account. Published rates and your contracted rates can differ substantially.
Planned: customs documentation beyond the commercial invoice, such as certificates of origin or dangerous goods paperwork, will not be generated.
Planned: FedEx Freight LTL services will not be in the first release; parcel and express only.
Planned: label voiding will follow FedEx's own cut-off rules, which means a label cannot always be cancelled even on the day it was created.

troubleshooting.error: Planned: Label creation fails with account not certified
troubleshooting.cause: The application has not passed FedEx production certification for that service.
troubleshooting.fix: Complete FedEx's certification process for the services you intend to use. Sandbox access does not imply production access.

troubleshooting.error: Planned: Rates returned are much higher than expected
troubleshooting.cause: The rating call is returning published rates because negotiated rates are not associated with the account.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask your FedEx account executive to enable negotiated rates on the API account, then re-run the rate request.

troubleshooting.error: Planned: Export label rejected for missing harmonised code
troubleshooting.cause: One or more line items on the consignment have no HS code on the item master.
troubleshooting.fix: Set harmonised codes on the item master. This is a customs requirement and we will block the label rather than let a shipment fail at the border.

troubleshooting.error: Planned: Third-party billing rejected
troubleshooting.cause: The customer's FedEx account number is wrong or does not permit third-party billing from your account.
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm the account number and the billing authorisation with the customer. FedEx will not accept a third-party bill the account holder has not permitted.

troubleshooting.error: Planned: Label cannot be voided
troubleshooting.cause: The shipment has passed FedEx's void cut-off, or has already been scanned.
troubleshooting.fix: Follow FedEx's return process. A scanned label cannot be voided and no integration changes that.

faqs.q: Why is the most-requested connector the last one?
faqs.a: Because label generation, rating, customs documentation and certification is a large piece of work, and doing it partly would be worse than not doing it. The date is Q2 2027 and we would rather publish an uncomfortable date than a comfortable fiction.

faqs.q: What do I do until then?
faqs.a: Use FedEx Ship Manager and record the tracking number on the order manually. It is not elegant and we are not going to pretend it is.

faqs.q: Which tiers will include it?
faqs.a: Professional and Enterprise, alongside the other logistics connectors.

faqs.q: Will it handle exports?
faqs.a: That is the plan, including commercial invoice data, harmonised codes and incoterms. Certificates of origin and dangerous goods documentation are out of scope.

faqs.q: Will it support FedEx Freight LTL?
faqs.a: Not in the first release. Parcel and express first, LTL later if demand justifies it.

faqs.q: Could the date move?
faqs.a: Yes, in either direction. When it moves, this page and the roadmap change on the same day, with the reason recorded in the changelog.
